data.label: grace:~/git/gbcli

data.title: gbcli: agent-friendly Game Boy development tool
data.description: Root of the gbcli plan. Goal, architecture, binding decisions and fidelity rules are in project/2026-11-06-plan.md; the evidence is in project/2026-11-06-backend-evaluation.md. Read both before claiming any leaf.

data.title: Stage 0: Foundations
Scaffold the repo with vendored SameBoy compiled by cgo
data.description:
Why: every later leaf builds on a Go module that compiles SameBoy's core with a plain `go build`, with no make, cppp or rgbds step. The evaluation found SameBoy's own `make lib` unusable on macOS (the dylib exports zero symbols; without the cppp tool the headers come out empty while make exits 0), and that compiling `Core/*.c` directly with `-DGB_INTERNAL` takes about 3.3 s and works.

What: a Go module (the user chose Go for the harness; see project/2026-11-06-plan.md, Decisions). SameBoy's `Core/` is vendored at a pinned commit (ea667ad was evaluated; take the latest master at the time, and record the commit and the reason in a short doc) with its LICENSE, compiled by cgo from a package directory. Flags from the evaluation are `-std=gnu11 -O2 -D_GNU_SOURCE -DGB_INTERNAL -DGB_VERSION=... -DGB_COPYRIGHT_YEAR=... -Wno-multichar`. SameBoy's open-source boot ROMs (Expat; `.asm` sources in BootROMs/) are built once with RGBDS by a script in scripts/ and the binaries committed, so a normal build needs no RGBDS. Never commit Nintendo boot ROM dumps.

Also check the debugger agent's suspicion that debugger.c tests `DISABLE_REWIND` where the build defines `GB_DISABLE_REWIND`, and decide whether we compile with the debugger or rewind disabled (we don't use SameBoy's debugger, but `debugger_ticks` lives behind it; we keep our own counter anyway).

The repo is not yet a git repository; initializing it and the .gitignore is part of this leaf if the user has not done it.

Out of scope: any wrapper logic. A smoke test only.

Risks: cgo compiles every .c in the package directory, so the vendored layout matters; SameBoy headers may need include-path care. Record the first-build time in AGENTS.md's head, since delegation sizing depends on build cost.

criteria.label: `go build ./...` succeeds on a clean checkout with no RGBDS, cppp or SDL installed
A Go test boots a ROM headless for 60 frames and asserts nothing was written to stdout
The vendored commit, its license notice and the boot ROM build script are in the repo, and the pinned commit is recorded in a dated doc
First clean build time and incremental build time are recorded in the AGENTS.md head

data.title: Kick the tires: DX note from a real homebrew task with existing tools
data.description:
Why: the house CLI rules (project/agents/cli-design.md, Building one) say to use the nearest existing tool for a real task, as an agent would, before designing verbs. The findings become the design doc's acceptance criteria.

What: a dated DX note in project/ pairing each friction point with the rule it implies. Do a small but real task the way our target agent would: write a tiny RGBDS program (a sprite that moves, with an OAM DMA routine), build it, then debug and measure it with existing tools: SameBoy's SDL debugger or Tester, and PyBoy 2.9's Python API (hooks, `memory[bank, addr]`, `tick`). Note what was slow, what needed a terminal or window, what answers were unstructured, what a cycle measurement took, and what you'd want in one round trip.

Needs RGBDS on PATH; if it's missing, ask the user to install it (it is also gbcli's own pinned dependency).

Out of scope: designing the protocol (the next leaf does that, informed by this note).

criteria.label: A dated DX note exists in project/ with at least ten findings, each paired with the rule it implies
The note records the exact tools, versions and commands used

data.title: Test-ROM corpus: pinned sources, licenses and a manifest
data.description:
Why: fidelity is the top priority, and the only way to protect it is a pinned corpus with known expected results. The shim's runner (stage 1) and any future bespoke core are measured against it.

What: a manifest (one row per ROM: suite, path, hardware model, pass-detection rule, license) and a script in scripts/ that fetches pinned versions. Suites to consider: blargg (cpu_instrs, instr_timing, mem_timing, dmg_sound, oam_bug, halt_bug), mooneye-test-suite, dmg-acid2 and cgb-acid2, mealybug-tearoom-tests, SameSuite, GateBoy gbmicrotests, age-test-roms, and docboy's own suite (2,949 DMG cases; see tests/config/dmg.json in docboy). Pass rules differ: mooneye signals with Fibonacci registers or serial, blargg with serial or memory text, acid tests with a reference framebuffer.

Also extract SameBoy's and docboy's per-test failures from https://gbdev.io/GBEmulatorShootout/ (the page is about 1 MB; read it in pieces). That tells us which hardware edges SameBoy misses, which feeds the bespoke-core decision.

Decide per suite whether ROMs may be committed or must be fetched. If any suite's license is unclear, fetch it rather than commit it, and flag it to the user.

Out of scope: the runner (stage 1, after the shim exists).

criteria.label: A manifest lists every ROM with suite, model, pass rule and license
The fetch script reproduces the corpus from pinned commits or hashes, verified by checksum
A dated doc lists SameBoy's and docboy's shootout failures test by test

data.title: Design doc: core C interface, protocol, sessions and CLI grammar
data.description:
Why: the protocol and the core interface are the expensive things to change later, and several user rulings must be turned into concrete shapes before stages 1–3 build them. This leaf needs the user's review; it is labeled decision.

What: a dated design doc in project/ covering:
- The core C interface, designed for the ideal core (the user's ruling; see project/2026-11-06-plan.md, Architecture). Include capability queries and explicit unsupported results for what SameBoy can't do (dot stepping, per-pixel layer identity).
- Run budgets (ticks, instructions, frames) and the stop-record schema: reason, PC, bank, emulated time.
- Direct-access regions and the three write kinds (bus write, poke, ROM patch).
- Taps (writes to the sound registers, PPU mode changes, scanlines).
- The JSONL envelope: request id, ok or error, error codes mapped to the house exit-code table, a remedy in every error, revision tokens on reads that precede mutations.
- Sessions: naming, the Unix socket location, listing and pruning, idle timeout, and the written daemon trigger.
- The checkpoint envelope and its exact verification rules, including ROM patches across save and load, loading a checkpoint taken under a previous ROM build, and model-family switches.
- The address grammar: `bank:addr`, `region:offset`, symbols.
- The condition-expression language. It must be side-effect free; consider SameBoy's syntax for familiarity, but evaluate over direct access.
- The experiment request: restore → patch → input → run to stop → measure → observe in one round trip. Batches follow the house rules: apply what can be applied; forward references by tag.
- CLI grammar: binary name (gbcli vs gb), verb classes, the primer, help topics, recipes. Rows by default, `--json` for the machine shape.
- Determinism contract, event log and gap ledger.

Inputs: the DX note (dxnote), project/agents/cli-design.md, the evaluation doc.

Out of scope: implementation.

Open questions for the user, to settle in review: binary name; whether a checkpoint loaded under a rebuilt ROM is refused or rebased by symbols; default budgets.

criteria.label: A dated design doc covers every bullet above, and each DX-note finding maps to a rule or a deliberate exception
The user has reviewed it and the open questions are answered in the doc

data.title: Stage 1: Core interface and SameBoy shim
Implement the core C interface over SameBoy: headless, deterministic, budgeted
data.description:
Why: this layer decides fidelity and speed for everything above it. The evaluation (project/2026-11-06-backend-evaluation.md, SameBoy section) lists the traps this leaf must close.

What: the shim implements the core C interface from the design doc over vendored SameBoy:
- Replace the log, input and async-input callbacks; SameBoy's defaults read our stdin and print to stdout.
- Turbo uncapped (`GB_set_turbo_mode(gb,true,true)`, `GB_set_turbo_cap(gb,0)`), because GB_run otherwise sleeps to real time.
- RNG seeded per instance before `GB_init` (the seed is process-global; serialize instance creation).
- RTC in accurate mode; joypad bounce off by default.
- Model and boot ROM selection.
- Budgeted runs that return stop records, and an emulated-time counter summed from `GB_run`'s 8 MHz ticks. Don't trust `GB_run_frame`'s return value; it summed to 0 in the bench, and the cause is unknown.
- A copy of the last completed frame at each `NORMAL_FRAME` vblank, separate from the live, partial buffer; raw DMG shades via a sentinel palette.
- The direct-access region table.
- Bus write vs poke vs ROM patch; state blob save and load.
- Explicit unsupported for what SameBoy can't do. Detect an illegal opcode before SameBoy locks the CPU (it sets IE=0 and halts without entering any debugger).

Tests drive the interface from Go. TDD red/green per the house rules.

Seams: the design doc's interface header; scaffold's cgo package. Out of scope: breakpoint and watchpoint filters (next leaf), anything in Go beyond tests.

criteria.label: Two instances with the same seed, ROM and inputs reach byte-identical states after 600 frames of cpu_instrs (test)
Throughput with rendering on is at least 18x realtime on cpu_instrs, against the 21.8x baseline from scripts/bench (benchmark recorded with command)
Restoring a checkpoint and running one frame takes under 1 ms (benchmark)
Every inspection call leaves the state hash unchanged, proven by hashing the state before and after each one (test)
Nothing reaches stdout during any test

data.title: Bank-aware breakpoint and watchpoint filters in C
data.description:
Why: the debugger needs per-instruction checks, but a Go callback per instruction would roughly halve speed (measured: C→Go 38.8 ns vs ≈44 ns of SameBoy work per instruction). So the check is a bitmap lookup in C that calls Go only on a match.

What: bank-aware bitmaps for execution, read and write. Execution is checked against PC and the current bank *before* each `GB_run`, so an execution stop lands before the instruction runs. Reads and writes are checked in SameBoy's memory callbacks; the write callback can veto a write. Stop records carry the reason, the address, the old and new values, PC, bank and emulated time.

Known hook gaps to document, not paper over: the write callback misses OAM DMA and HDMA destination writes; the execution callback can't veto and doesn't fire for interrupt dispatch; the read callback also fires for the core's own "safe" reads. SameBoy's own banked-SRAM/VRAM watchpoint bug does not apply to us, because we compute banks ourselves (prove it with a test).

Out of scope: condition evaluation (in Go, stage 2).

criteria.label: With 1,000 armed but non-matching filters, throughput drops by no more than 10% (benchmark)
A breakpoint on a banked address fires only in that bank, and a watchpoint on banked cart RAM fires (tests)
A write veto leaves memory unchanged and reports the attempted value (test)

data.title: Test-ROM runner over the core interface; record the SameBoy baseline
data.description:
Why: closes stage 1. The baseline guards the shim against regressions and is the yardstick for any future core.

What: a runner (Go test or command under scripts/) that runs every corpus ROM through the core interface, applies the manifest's pass rule and writes a results file. Calibrate it against a known answer before trusting it: our results must match SameBoy's published claims (all of mooneye and blargg pass), allowing for boot-ROM-dependent tests, which need Nintendo's original boot ROMs that we don't ship. Explain every difference.

Out of scope: fixing SameBoy bugs.

criteria.label: A committed baseline file lists pass or fail per ROM per model, with the command that produced it
Every difference from SameBoy's published results is explained in a dated note
The runner runs in CI or as a documented single command

data.title: Stage 2: Engine (Go library)
Sessions and checkpoints: envelope, identity, patches, ROM reload
data.description:
Why: the fast feedback loop (restore, try, restore) is the user's central requirement, and checkpoints are its unit.

What: an engine session owns one or more core instances. Named checkpoints live in memory; export and import to disk use the checkpoint envelope from the design doc (SameBoy blob + ROM hash, core commit, model, boot ROM hash, config, emulated cycles, ROM patch set, key state, debugger configuration).
- Loading verifies the envelope first and refuses mismatches with an error that names the remedy. SameBoy itself would silently switch models within a family and checks no ROM identity.
- Reloading a rebuilt ROM while keeping a checkpoint: use the old and new .sym files to detect a stale PC or stale return addresses on the stack, and refuse unless told otherwise (the design doc settles the exact rule).
- Cloning an instance for A/B experiments; SameBoy supports several instances per process.

Out of scope: the protocol.

criteria.label: A save, mutate, restore cycle returns a byte-identical state blob and envelope (test)
Loading a checkpoint whose ROM hash or model differs is refused with a remedy (tests per mismatch kind)
Reloading a rebuilt ROM whose symbols moved under the saved PC is refused and names the moved symbol (test)

data.title: Debugger: conditions, stepping, stop reasons, symbols, disassembler
data.description:
Why: a debugger that agents can drive without a terminal, built on our filters, because SameBoy's own debugger can't be used headless and perturbs DMG state (evaluation doc, Debugger).

What:
- Conditional breakpoints and read/write watchpoints using the design doc's expression language: registers, memory (read through direct access only), old and new values, banked addresses, symbols.
- Stepping: instruction, over, out, frame, scanline (run until LY changes), run-until-address.
- Typed stop reasons: breakpoint, watchpoint, step done, budget exhausted, illegal opcode, HALT with interrupts off, user break.
- rgbds .sym loading.
- A disassembler in Go that returns structured instructions (length, cycles, operands, symbol annotations), built from a sourced opcode table (e.g. the gbdev opcode JSON; cite it next to the table). SameBoy's disassembler only prints text.
- A backtrace from a shadow call stack is a should, if the execution hook makes it cheap.

Out of scope: protocol formatting.

criteria.label: A condition that reads memory leaves the state hash unchanged when it is evaluated (test)
Every stop reason has a test that produces it and checks the record's PC, bank and emulated time
The disassembler matches the sourced opcode table for all 512 opcodes, including length and cycles (test)

data.title: Inspection: registers, regions, decoded hardware registers, PPU and APU state
data.description:
Why: agents need complete, faithful reads, and some raw IO bytes are not the register's value (evaluation doc, Inspection: DIV, TIMA during reload, JOYP, NRxx).

What: reads of registers (including IME and halted), every direct-access region by name, bank and offset, and every ROM and RAM bank. A decoded hardware-register table that marks which values are derived. Structured tile, tilemap and OAM data (not images; those are stage 4). APU channel state from SameBoy's public getters.

criteria.label: Every documented hardware register has a decoder test, including DIV and TIMA during reload
Reads of every bank of ROM, cart RAM, WRAM and VRAM match the backing memory (test)

data.title: Stage 3: Server, client and CLI
JSONL server and named sessions over a Unix socket

criteria.label: A golden test drives a scripted JSONL session over stdio and over a socket and asserts the exact response bytes
A request that would run without a budget gets the default budget, and the stop record says so (test)
Gap-ledger counts appear in the event log after an unsupported request (test)

data.title: The CLI: verbs, primer, help, recipes, exit codes
data.description:
Why: the agent-facing surface. House rules in project/agents/cli-design.md apply in full.

What: the thin client verbs from the design doc. A bare invocation prints a primer; each verb's `--help` carries a worked example; `help <topic>` and `help recipes` follow the woodcase pattern. Output is rows by default, with `--json`. The shared exit-code table applies. Every error names the thing, what happened and the next command. The experiment request is available as one verb. Tests drive the binary against fixture ROMs in a temp directory and assert bytes and exit codes; every error path has a test that reads its remedy.

Closes stage 3.

criteria.label: Every verb has a golden test of its default and --json output, and every error type has a test asserting its remedy text
The CLI client starts and completes a trivial request against a live session in under 50 ms (benchmark)

data.title: CI on macOS and Linux
data.description:
Why: open source, macOS first and Linux ideal (user ruling). CI keeps the Linux build honest from early on.

What: CI building and testing on macOS arm64 and Linux x86_64 (and arm64 if cheap), running the test suite and the test-ROM runner once it exists. SameBoy's core is portable C; watch for `_GNU_SOURCE` and clang/gcc differences.

criteria.label: CI passes on macOS and Linux for the default branch

data.title: Stage 4: Observations
Screenshots and visual views
data.description:
Why: vision models need faithful, pixel-exact images, and cheaper structured views first (house rule: every read has a cheaper sibling).

What:
- PNG at native resolution and integer scales, default 4×, nearest neighbor, no smoothing; crops.
- The last completed frame vs the live partial frame, labeled.
- Filmstrips and atlases over N frames for animation.
- Tileset, tilemap (the full 256×256 map with the viewport rectangle drawn on it) and OAM views.
- A frame-diff view.

Output is deterministic, pinned by golden images.

criteria.label: Golden-image tests pin native and 4x output, crops, a filmstrip and each debug view
A screenshot request never advances emulation (state hash test)

data.title: Audio views: APU write log, WAV, piano roll, spectrogram
data.description:
Why: audio debugging for agents, cheapest view first (user discussion, 2026-11-06).

What:
- A log of writes to the sound registers, stamped with emulated time (from the write tap or SameBoy's VGM writer), decoded into channel, note, envelope, duty and trigger.
- WAV export, mixed and per channel. Per channel comes from SameBoy's amplitude getters or a muted replay from a checkpoint; verify that the replay is exactly deterministic before relying on it.
- A piano-roll PNG with one lane per channel.
- A spectrogram PNG per channel and mixed.

Whether vision models actually benefit from the spectrogram is a question for the agent eval.

criteria.label: The decoded write log for a known test tune matches a hand-checked expectation (test)
Per-channel WAVs sum to the mixed output within a stated tolerance, or the doc explains why not (test)

data.title: Stage 5: Profiling and verification
Cycle profiler and raster timeline
data.description:
Why: the target use case is aggressive optimization. The agent needs exact cycle costs and to see where in the frame and scanline its code runs.

What:
- Emulated cycles between two points.
- Cycles per routine by .sym (execution hook plus shadow stack).
- Per-frame budget: active vs HALT time; lag frames, with a written definition.
- A per-scanline timeline: PPU mode transitions from the LCD status and line callbacks, and register writes with their dot position.

Dot positions come from emulated time relative to the line start; if SameBoy's granularity limits this, say so with an explicit *unsupported* plus a gap-ledger entry rather than guessing.

criteria.label: Cycle counts for hand-written test routines match hand-computed values from the opcode table (tests)
The raster timeline for a mid-scanline effect test ROM places the writes on the expected lines (test)

data.title: Equivalence check: A/B ROMs from the same state and inputs
data.description:
Why: the guardrail that makes "unbelievably performant" safe. An optimized ROM must behave the same as the original.

What: run two ROMs (or one ROM with and without a patch) from equivalent checkpoints with the same scripted input timeline. Compare frames, chosen RAM ranges and the audio write log, and report the first divergence with emulated time and both states. Checkpoints taken under different ROM builds need the design doc's rebuilt-ROM rule.

criteria.label: A deliberately broken optimization is caught with the exact first divergent frame (test)
A known-equivalent rewrite passes over 600 frames of scripted input (test)

data.title: Stage 6: Build loop and onboarding
doctor, build and new: the RGBDS loop
data.description:
Why: closes edit → build → restore → measure in one command (user ruling: RGBDS first, from PATH, checked against a pinned version).

What:
- `doctor` checks the RGBDS version against the pin and prints the install command.
- `build` runs rgbasm, rgblink and rgbfix and turns their diagnostics into structured errors (file, line, message). It optionally reloads the result into a session at a named checkpoint, subject to the rebuilt-ROM rule.
- `new` scaffolds a minimal starter project: header, a pinned hardware.inc, an OAM DMA routine in HRAM, a VBlank handler and a build file. It builds and runs on the first try.

GBDK is in the backlog, not here.

criteria.label: `new` then `build` then a screenshot succeeds on a clean machine with only the pinned RGBDS installed (test)
A deliberate syntax error comes back as a structured error with file and line (test)

data.title: Onboarding content: cheat sheet, lookups, traps with demo ROMs
data.description:
Why: the user's lens is "what does a Sonnet-class model need to get productive with GB development through our CLI". This is not a course; link out to Pan Docs and gbdev for depth.

What, as `help` topics and recipes:
- A one-page hardware cheat sheet: memory map, PPU modes and access windows, frame and scanline budgets, interrupts. Each figure cites a Pan Docs section.
- A lookup verb for instruction cycles and sizes from the sourced opcode table.
- The dev-loop recipes.
- Traps that models fall into, each with a small demo ROM run in CI: VRAM writes in mode 3, LCD off outside VBlank, the HALT bug, OAM DMA not in HRAM, RGBDS version syntax changes.
- Go-deeper links pinned to specific Pan Docs sections.

Size it by the eval, not by guesswork: start small.

criteria.label: Every figure in the cheat sheet cites its source, and every trap has a demo ROM checked in CI

data.title: Stage 7: Agent eval
Agent eval: a fresh Sonnet-class agent builds and optimizes with gbcli
data.description:
Why: the definition of done for the CLI and onboarding, and the evidence for the bespoke-core decision.

What: give a fresh Sonnet-class agent only the gbcli binary and a task. For example: make a sprite move at 60 fps, then cut the main loop's cycles by 30% without changing behavior, proven by the equivalence check. Record every stumble and turn each into a recipe, cheat-sheet line, error remedy or verb change; repeat until a run completes without avoidable stumbles. Read the gap ledger at the end and summarize it for the bespoke decision. Also assess whether the spectrogram and piano roll helped.

Write the results as a dated doc in project/.

criteria.label: A dated eval doc records each run, its stumbles and the fix for each
A final run completes the task with no stumble attributable to gbcli's docs or errors
The gap-ledger summary is in the eval doc

data.title: Stage 8: Bespoke core decision
Decide: spike a bespoke Rust core now, or park it

criteria.label: A dated decision doc records the evidence, the choice and either the spike plan or the backlog entry with its un-park condition

data.title: Stage 9: Cartridges
Mapper coverage and header checks
data.description:
Why: games built with gbcli must work on real carts (cart research in the evaluation doc). Must-haves: MBC5 (bank 0 selectable, 9-bit bank, up to 128 KiB RAM, the rumble bit), ROM-only, battery SRAM saved to .sav, MBC3 with RTC (deterministic in accurate mode). Should: MBC1 and MBC1M. FRAM behaves as non-volatile RAM.

What: tests for each must-have mapper through the core interface, using mapper test ROMs from the corpus where they exist (e.g. mooneye's emulator-only MBC tests). Warnings when the header's cart type, ROM size or RAM size disagree with the file. Battery saves persisted alongside sessions.

criteria.label: Mapper test ROMs for MBC1, MBC3 and MBC5 pass, or each failure is explained (runner results)
A ROM whose header disagrees with its size triggers a warning with a remedy (test)

data.title: Parameterized flash-chip model for flash-save carts
data.description:
Why: GB Studio's batteryless saves write to the cart's flash chip, and no emulator checked models that. Boards also differ, so a fixed model would hide the bugs that matter.

What: an AMD/JEDEC flash model built on SameBoy's write hook (which can veto) and read hook (which can replace values). It handles program, sector and chip erase, reset, autoselect, and busy-status reads (DQ7/DQ6 toggle). Parameters: unlock addresses ($AAA, $555, $5555, $4AAA variants), D0/D1 data-line swap, sector map, /WE on WR vs AUDIO, and busy duration. Named profiles come from the FlashGBX cart database (lesserkuma/FlashGBX config/fc_DMG_*.txt).

Validate with a GB Studio batteryless build: it should save and restore on a swapped-data profile, and fail on an unswapped one, as the evaluation infers.

Out of scope: Intel command sets and CPLD multicart mappers (could-haves).

criteria.label: A GB Studio batteryless ROM saves and restores across a power cycle under a swapped-data profile (test)
The same ROM's save fails under an unswapped profile, and the failure is reported clearly (test)

data.new_desc:
Why: every later leaf builds on a Rust workspace that compiles SameBoy's core with a plain `cargo build`, with no make, cppp or rgbds step. The evaluation found SameBoy's own `make lib` unusable on macOS (the dylib exports zero symbols; without the cppp tool the headers come out empty while make exits 0), and that compiling `Core/*.c` directly with `-DGB_INTERNAL` takes about 3.3 s and works. The harness language is Rust (user ruling, 2026-11-06; first decided as Go and changed the same day — project/2026-11-06-backend-evaluation.md, Language, correction).

What: a Cargo workspace shaped for fast incremental builds: small crates so that touching the CLI does not recompile the engine. A proposed split (the builder may adjust and say why): a `sys` crate (vendored SameBoy plus a few C accessor functions for internal fields such as IME, compiled by the `cc` crate; hand-written FFI declarations for the functions we use, no bindgen), a `core` crate (the core trait; the SameBoy backend may live here or in its own crate), `engine`, `protocol`, and the `gbcli` binary. No async runtime.

SameBoy's `Core/` is vendored at a pinned commit (ea667ad was evaluated; take the latest master at the time, and record the commit and the reason in a short dated doc) with its LICENSE. Flags from the evaluation: `-std=gnu11 -O2 -D_GNU_SOURCE -DGB_INTERNAL -DGB_VERSION=... -DGB_COPYRIGHT_YEAR=... -Wno-multichar`. SameBoy's open-source boot ROMs (Expat; `.asm` sources in BootROMs/) are built once with RGBDS (installed: rgbasm v1.0.4) by a script in scripts/ and the binaries committed, so a normal build needs no RGBDS. Never commit Nintendo boot ROM dumps.

Dependencies: the house rule is to ask before adding each one. Pre-approved by the plan's direction: `cc` (build), `serde` + `serde_json` (protocol), `png` (screenshots, later). Anything else, including an argument parser, asks the user first.

Also check the debugger agent's suspicion that debugger.c tests `DISABLE_REWIND` where the build defines `GB_DISABLE_REWIND`, and decide whether to compile with SameBoy's debugger or rewind disabled. We don't use SameBoy's debugger; `debugger_ticks` lives behind it, but we keep our own counter anyway.

Build speed is a design constraint, not an afterthought: the toy-crate benchmark (scripts/bench/rust-build) measured 4.6 s incremental debug, which does not predict scaling. Record real numbers and add a small script in scripts/ that re-measures them, so later leaves can watch for regressions.

Out of scope: any wrapper logic. A smoke test only.

data.old_desc:

What: the shim implements the core C interface from the design doc over vendored SameBoy:

- Turbo uncapped (`GB_set_turbo_mode(gb,true,true)`, `GB_set_turbo_cap(gb,0)`), because GB_run otherwise sleeps to real time.
- RNG seeded per instance before `GB_init` (the seed is process-global; serialize instance creation).
- RTC in accurate mode; joypad bounce off by default.
- Model and boot ROM selection.
- Budgeted runs that return stop records, and an emulated-time counter summed from `GB_run`'s 8 MHz ticks. Don't trust `GB_run_frame`'s return value; it summed to 0 in the bench, and the cause is unknown.
- A copy of the last completed frame at each `NORMAL_FRAME` vblank, separate from the live, partial buffer; raw DMG shades via a sentinel palette.
- The direct-access region table.
- Bus write vs poke vs ROM patch; state blob save and load.
- Explicit unsupported for what SameBoy can't do. Detect an illegal opcode before SameBoy locks the CPU (it sets IE=0 and halts without entering any debugger).

data.old_desc:
Why: the debugger needs per-instruction checks, but a Go callback per instruction would roughly halve speed (measured: C→Go 38.8 ns vs ≈44 ns of SameBoy work per instruction). So the check is a bitmap lookup in C that calls Go only on a match.

What: bank-aware bitmaps for execution, read and write. Execution is checked against PC and the current bank *before* each `GB_run`, so an execution stop lands before the instruction runs. Reads and writes are checked in SameBoy's memory callbacks; the write callback can veto a write. Stop records carry the reason, the address, the old and new values, PC, bank and emulated time.

Known hook gaps to document, not paper over: the write callback misses OAM DMA and HDMA destination writes; the execution callback can't veto and doesn't fire for interrupt dispatch; the read callback also fires for the core's own "safe" reads. SameBoy's own banked-SRAM/VRAM watchpoint bug does not apply to us, because we compute banks ourselves (prove it with a test).

Out of scope: condition evaluation (in Go, stage 2).

DX scout done (2026-11-06). Full DX note returned to the main thread as text; artifacts in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ben-git-gbcli/a957b173-5765-4a04-b8cf-1b1964b94a03/scratchpad/dx/ (src/main.asm, py/session.py, harness/sbh.c, sbrun/s5.txt).

Headline findings:
- Program (164-line asm, 275 B ROM0) built clean first try with rgbasm 1.0.4 + gbdev hardware.inc v4.9.1 (v4 pinned deliberately: v5 renames constants).
- PyBoy 2.9: works headless, ~6 ms warm restore->30 frames->screenshot, but: no cycle counter in the public API (I parsed cpu.cycles out of a save state at byte 25), hooking a HALT silently hangs forever, HRAM can't be hooked ("Invalid memory address for bank"), no watchpoints, Pillow is an undeclared dependency (screen.image returns a sentinel), RAM is zeroed (unlike hardware).
- SameBoy: tester builds in 7 s and screenshots (BMP, after N seconds incl. boot), but can't answer anything else. SDL debugger is unusable headless: needs a window server (fails in sandbox; dummy driver fails because the window is always created with SDL_WINDOW_OPENGL), and the piped-stdin path spins on EOF. `make lib` "succeeds" with all-empty public headers because `cppp` is missing and the pipe swallows the error.
- An 86-line C harness on libsameboy.a (Core/ headers) answered everything: `ticks` gave 164 T / 41 M-cycles for the main loop (matches the hand count and PyBoy's 152+12), watchpoints on $FF46 and wSpriteX stopped with backtrace, save/poke/restore/compare, and loading a v2 ROM under an old state worked. Warm round trip ~22-25 ms per 30 frames (~1500 fps turbo); fresh process 20-30 ms vs PyBoy 300+ ms.
- Plausible-wrong answers I actually hit: "frame 60" screenshot was the PyBoy boot logo; run-until predicates on uninitialized WRAM (SameBoy randomizes it) passed instantly ("ran 0 frames"); a screenshot taken during LCD-off was all white with exit 0; screen pixels lag OAM/WRAM by one frame and the two emulators stop at different points relative to the game's frame counter; SameBoy without turbo silently runs at real time (400 frames = 6.7 s).

data.new_desc:
Why: both client kinds (user ruling): harness code speaks JSONL over stdio; an agent in a shell needs a named, persistent session it can reach from separate commands. The design doc (project/2026-11-06-design.md §1, user-approved 2026-11-06) chose a session bundle on disk over a daemon: a fresh process costs ~25-30 ms per round trip, dominated by emulation, so a daemon bought only retained state.

What: the session bundle store and `gbcli serve` (JSONL over stdio). Per design §1, §5, §10:

- Bundle layout under ./.gbcli/ (found by walking up from the cwd; GBCLI_DIR overrides): sessions/<name>/{session.json, head.gbck, history/, checkpoints/, events.jsonl, lock}, cache/boot-*.gbck, gaps.jsonl.
- Each command: flock the session, restore the head, apply the request, write the new head atomically (temp + rename), rotate history (last 8), append to the event log. A second writer waits within its budget, then session_busy (exit 3).
- Revision counter per session; mutating requests may pass rev; mismatch is rev_mismatch (exit 3).
- Sessions: named ([a-z0-9-]{1,40}), naming creates; `sessions` lists rows; `sessions prune --unused-for <dur>` and `sessions rm` (refuses with named checkpoints unless --with-checkpoints). No idle timeout (nothing stays running).
- `serve`: one engine in memory for the life of stdin; may load from and save to a named session. One crate of request and response types (serde) shared by server and CLI. stdout carries protocol only; diagnostics to stderr; streamed events flushed per line.
- Every run has a budget (default 600 frames for run --until/--to; 60 s wall guard); inspection never advances emulation.
- The error-code enum maps each code to one house exit code, and every error has a remedy (design §5).
- Event log and gap ledger per design §10.

No Unix socket and no daemon. The revive trigger is written in design §1: bundle overhead >10% of a typical round trip, or a feature needs live push.

data.text:
Backend built (crates/sameboy, gbcli-sameboy) over the core trait (crates/core). Findings worth keeping:
- GB_set_rtc_mode stamps last_rtc_second = time(NULL) (timing.c:330) and that field is in the save state, so two instances built a second apart differed. Shim gbcli_clear_rtc_epoch pins it to 0; regression test host_time_does_not_reach_the_state (fails without the fix).
- SameBoy's live framebuffer isn't in its save state: after a mid-frame load the first frame keeps stale lines. The core blob now carries the live screen (w*h pixels) plus ticks, vblank count and the last complete frame.
- GB_run_frame anomaly explained: with turbo and cap 0, GB_timing_sync (called from GB_display_vblank, display.c:311) zeroes cycles_since_last_sync at the vblank that ends the frame, so GB_run_frame returns ~0.
- PPU dot not readable (cycles_for_line resets to 0 in mode 0 and stays 0 on lines 144-153); probed, recorded in design §2.2.
- Illegal-opcode check before each GB_run cost 12% throughput as written; restructured (ROM fast path + table, full conditions only when the byte at PC is illegal) it costs ~8%.
- Build flags: the 21.8x baseline was SameBoy's `make lib CONF=release` = -O3 -ffast-math -DNDEBUG -flto. Our cc build was -O2 with asserts on: the same C bench loop linked against it ran ~17.9x. Now -O3 -DNDEBUG (no fast-math, no LTO): C loop ~21x, our backend 19.2-19.4x.
- Key changes (GB_set_key_mask) reach JOYP on the next emulated cycle, not immediately.
Throughput: cargo run --release -p gbcli-sameboy --example bench -- tests/corpus/fetched/blargg/cpu_instrs/cpu_instrs.gb -> 18.7-19.4x (3600 frames, render on, load avg ~2.3-3 on 8 CPUs). Restore + one frame of ticks: mean 0.645 ms, worst 0.70-0.75 ms over 1000.

Built in crates/sameboy/src/watch.rs and run.rs; tests in crates/sameboy/tests/filters.rs on our own ROM crates/sameboy/tests/roms/banked.asm (MBC5, 4 ROM banks, 4 RAM banks).
- Exec filters are checked in the run loop before each GB_run (PC via the cached GB_get_registers pointer, bank via the shim's gbcli_bank_for); a run never stops on an exec hit before its first step, so resuming makes progress. Read/write filters run in SameBoy's memory callbacks, armed only while a request has them (an RAII guard disarms on every exit). The write callback vetoes via a new RunRequest::veto filter (design §2 update).
- Banks come from our shim, not SameBoy's debugger, so its 8000-CFFF-is-bank-0 bug doesn't apply: a_write_watch_on_banked_cart_ram_fires_in_its_bank... proves a cart-RAM watch in bank 2 fires and reports bank 2.
- Never-written tracking lives in the core (the write hook is there) with CPU and poke bitmaps for WRAM, HRAM, cart RAM; saved in the core blob; Core::written(region). VRAM/OAM -> Unsupported(WriteHookCoversDma).
Benchmarks, best of 6 interleaved runs each (machine shared, load avg 3-6): cargo run --release -p gbcli-sameboy --example bench -- tests/corpus/fetched/blargg/cpu_instrs/cpu_instrs.gb 3600 1 <mode>
  plain 19.2x, tracking 18.7x (-2.6%, under the 5% line: stays on by default), filters 17.7x (-7.8% with 1,000 armed non-matching filters on hot addresses, wrong banks: under the 10% line).

data.title: Structured disassembler from a sourced opcode table
data.description:
Why: the debugger, profiler and CLI need structured instructions, and SameBoy's disassembler only prints text (and is compiled out). Split out of mvsVA9 on 2026-11-06 because it is independent of checkpoints and filters, so it can run in parallel.

What: a disassembler in Rust in the engine crate that returns structured instructions (length, cycles taken and not taken, operands, and symbol annotations via an injected symbol lookup), built from a sourced opcode table such as the gbdev opcode JSON, cited next to the table. It covers all 256 base and 256 CB-prefixed opcodes. Illegal opcodes are marked as such.

criteria.label: The disassembler matches the sourced opcode table for all 512 opcodes, including length and cycles (test)

data.label: The disassembler matches the sourced opcode table for all 512 opcodes, including length and cycles (test)

data.text: The disassembler bullet and its criterion moved to a separate leaf under Stage 2 on 2026-11-06 (it is independent, so it runs in parallel). This leaf keeps conditions, stepping, stop reasons, .sym loading (which the checkpoint leaf CjBWCm may build first for the rebuilt-ROM check; reuse it) and the backtrace. Stop reasons here are the engine's stop record built on the core's Candidate hits (design §2 stage-1 update).

Shape after the approved design (project/2026-11-06-design.md §1, §6; user 2026-11-06): the engine library holds sessions and checkpoints in memory and encodes and decodes the `.gbck` envelope to and from bytes. Persisting to ./.gbcli/ is the bundle-store leaf IVPZ22, so this leaf writes no files except in tests. The envelope follows §6 exactly: the header fields, hashes of the unpatched ROM, a hand-written SHA-256 checked against NIST vectors, and the seven verification steps in order. Breakpoints, watches and taps are copied into the header for reference but not restored by default (fidelity rule 4 narrowed). The rebuilt-ROM rule is §6's symbol check: refuse when PC's symbol, a RAM symbol, a stack return address or a breakpoint symbol moved; warn otherwise; --allow-rom-change overrides; no .sym means refuse. That needs an RGBDS .sym parser, which this leaf builds as a module the debugger leaf reuses. The core's blob already carries ticks, the frame count, the never-written bitmaps and the live framebuffer (stage 1).

Built in crates/engine (uncommitted, worktree agent-ac8e8d8875384a5a2): Machine (Box<dyn Core> + unpatched ROM, boot ROM, seed, config, patches, keys, symbols, debugger config; Backend::sameboy() builds cores), Session (machines + named checkpoints, clone_machine, import/export), Checkpoint encode/decode (GBCK | u32 v1 | u32 len | JSON | blob), hand-written SHA-256 (NIST vectors), RGBDS .sym parser (sym.rs), the seven verification steps in Machine::restore with CheckpointError::remedy(), and the rebuilt-ROM check (romcheck.rs). CheckpointHeader lives in gbcli-protocol (design §6 names protocol::CheckpointHeader); core enums serialize through serde remote derives, compile-checked against the core.
Decisions: restore and clone rebuild the core from the unpatched ROM, apply the patch set in order (checking each patch's `before` bytes), then load the blob, so step 6 is exact by construction. symbols_live = PC's ROM symbol + every RAM symbol + ROM symbols under stack words (scan SP up to the next RAM symbol / area end / 128 bytes, stopping at a never-written byte). The header carries no full ROM symbol table, so the "loads with a warning" case says how many live symbols were checked rather than listing moved non-live ROM symbols (deviation, recorded in the design doc). `written` is not duplicated in the header: the core blob carries it (stage 1). created_by/parent are caller-supplied (SaveMeta).
Test ROMs: crates/engine/tests/roms/rebuild_v1..v4 (+ .sym), built by scripts/build-roms.sh (now also emits .sym for every test ROM).

Built gbcli_engine::inspect (crates/engine/src/inspect/: mod.rs cpu+apu_state, regions.rs, hwreg.rs, hwreg_table.rs, video.rs). Design doc §2.3 has an update block with the details.

Core (additive): Core::apu() -> ApuState (volume/amplitude/period per channel, wave table, sync Current|Lagging) with a default Unsupported(Feature::ApuChannels); new Feature::ApuChannels (Yes on SameBoy). SameBoy: gbcli_io_peek now mirrors read_high_memory + GB_apu_read for every IO address; Unsupported only for PPU-synced regs while mode 3 is batched and NR52/PCM12/34/wave-RAM-during-playback while apu.apu_cycles > 0.

Findings: GB_get_channel_edge_triggered clears the flag (not used). SameBoy APU state lags by up to max_cycles_per_sample (0x400 with no sample rate) between APU accesses, so NR52 rarely decodes at a random boundary; it always decodes right after any APU register access.

Criteria evidence: T4Y -> crates/engine/tests/inspect_hwreg.rs (every table register equals a bus read on a restored copy at 30 random points on DMG and on CGB and after an APU write, and each decodes at least once; DIV and TIMA-during-reload tests). i6W -> crates/engine/tests/inspect_regions.rs (every bank of ROM 4, cart RAM 4, WRAM 8, VRAM 2 on a CGB-mode MBC5 cart equals the CPU's view when mapped).

data.title: Per-pixel layer identity via a vendored SameBoy patch
data.description:
Why: the user expects layer identity ("which layer drew this pixel") to matter for the target use case: raster tricks and sprite-priority bugs in a tight DMG game. Today it is Feature::PixelLayers = No on SameBoy. Read on the main thread, 2026-11-06: SameBoy decides the winner of every pixel at one mixing point in Core/display.c (around lines 670-760, ea667ad: background/window FIFO pop, OAM FIFO pop, `draw_oam`, bg_priority) and then discards it.

What: a small, observation-only patch to the vendored display.c that writes a per-pixel layer tag (background, window, or object plus its OAM index) into an optional side buffer, enabled only while a request asks for it. The object index probably needs a field on SameBoy's OAM FIFO item, and window vs background may need a flag; verify both. Expose it through Core::pixel_layers() and flip Feature::PixelLayers to Yes on SameBoy. Record the patch in project/2026-11-06-sameboy-vendoring.md, keep it as a patch file reapplied by scripts/vendor-sameboy.sh, and consider offering it upstream to SameBoy.

Rejected alternatives (main-thread reading): replaying with GB_set_object/background_rendering_disabled changes object fetch and therefore mode-3 timing (display.c ~1181, ~1347), so the replay diverges. Re-rendering from VRAM/OAM is wrong under mid-line raster changes. Both violate "reject, don't approximate".

criteria.label: State and frames are byte-identical with the layer buffer on and off, over a busy ROM and cpu_instrs (test)
Layer tags are correct on dmg-acid2 and on a sprite-priority test ROM of our own (tests)
The patch is a file in the repo, reapplied by scripts/vendor-sameboy.sh, and documented in the vendoring doc
Throughput cost with the buffer off is under 1%, and with it on is measured and recorded

Built gbcli_engine::disasm (crates/engine/src/disasm/: mod.rs decode/Instruction/Operand/SymbolLookup, types.rs, table.rs generated).

Source: gbdev/gb-opcodes Opcodes.json at 376f61c86fdac2048f7ce5fe838ae756b306017e (2024-12-13), CC0-1.0, committed unmodified at crates/engine/data/gb-opcodes/ with LICENSE and SOURCE. scripts/disasm/gen_opcodes.py generates table.rs (python stdlib only); --check fails when table.rs is stale.

Choice: generate Rust with a script rather than parse at build time, because parsing at build time needs a JSON parser in build.rs (a new build dependency) or a hand-written one; generated Rust has no runtime or build cost and reviews as one line per opcode. The cross-check test (crates/engine/tests/disasm_table.rs) reads the JSON with serde_json as a dev-dependency only (approved list).

Symbol annotation: trait SymbolLookup { fn symbol(&self, addr: u16) -> Option<SymbolRef{name, offset}> }; the implementor owns bank context. Operands with an address (a16, a8 as FF00+n, JR targets, RST vectors) get the lookup's symbol, else the hardware register name from inspect::hwreg (rLCDC). n16 is not annotated (may be a constant).

Criterion 2DX evidence: all_512_opcodes_match_the_sourced_table checks mnemonic, length, taken/not-taken cycles, operand names and indirect/increment/decrement for every base and CB opcode against the JSON; a mutated cycle count in table.rs makes it fail (checked, then regenerated).

data.title: Predicate stops (--until) with cadence derived from the expression
data.description:
Why: `run --until <expr>` (design §11) is the core of "one round trip per question", but the engine leaf mvsVA9 left it unbuilt. Evaluating an arbitrary predicate after every instruction costs a lot of speed, and the cadence is a design choice.

Proposal (main thread, 2026-11-06), to confirm with the user: derive the cadence from what the expression reads. Memory-only predicates (the common case: `u16[wFrame] >= 60`) can only change when a referenced byte is written, so arm write candidates on exactly those addresses and evaluate on each hit. That is exact and nearly free. `frame` is evaluated at each vblank, and `ly` at each scanline change. Predicates on registers, `pc` or `t` are evaluated every instruction, which is exact but slow; the stop record notes the cost. A per-instruction fallback is always correct, so this is purely an optimization over a correct baseline. Never-written reads still refuse (§8). The Predicate stop reason joins the stop record.

criteria.label: A memory-only predicate stops on the exact instruction that made it true, at near-zero cost (test + benchmark)
Register and pc predicates stop exactly, with their cost measured and recorded

data.text:
Ruling (user, 2026-11-06): derive the cadence from what the predicate reads, with a
per-instruction fallback. Concretely:

- A static read whose address(es) the write hook covers (WRAM, HRAM, cart RAM, ROM,
  and IO that only changes on a CPU write) arms write candidates on exactly those
  addresses; the predicate is evaluated on each hit. Banked reads insert the bank,
  and echo RAM is canonicalized, so a banked WRAM/cart-RAM read fires only for the
  bank it names.
- `frame` is evaluated at each vblank; `ly` is checked cheaply after every
  instruction and evaluated only when LY changes.
- Everything else is evaluated after every instruction: registers, flags, `ime`,
  `pc`, `bank`, `t`, dynamic addresses (`[hl]`, `[wTable + b]`), VRAM and OAM
  reads (the write hook misses OAM DMA and HDMA destinations), and IO registers
  that change without a CPU write (`[rLY]`, `[rDIV]`, `[rTIMA]`, `[rIF]`,
  `[rSTAT]`). CPU-address reads in a switchable ROM bank fall here too, since a
  bank switch changes the value without a write to the address.

The per-instruction fallback is the correctness baseline; the derived triggers are
an exact optimization over it. The Predicate stop record carries the predicate text
and the cadence used, so the cost is visible in the response.

Leaf MBSvZS built `--until` predicate stops with the cadence derived from the expression.

WHAT LANDED
- `gbcli_protocol::Cadence` (Writes < Vblank < Scanline < EveryInstruction) and `StopReason::Predicate { text, cadence }`; serde snake_case, and the stop record carries the cost.
- `Condition::cadence()` plus a private analysis in `crates/engine/src/cond/cadence.rs`: static CPU reads arm one write candidate per byte (width 2 arms both, wrapping at $FFFF), banked reads insert their bank, region offsets map to CPU addresses, echo RAM canonicalizes, and the fine cases (registers, `pc`, `t`, `bank`, dynamic addresses, VRAM/OAM, PPU-synced IO, a CPU address in ROMX) fall back to `every_instruction`.
- `Machine::run_until(&mut self, predicate, opts)`, `DebugError::{UntilSyntax, Until}` (`until: …`, not `condition of #0`), and the run loop triggers: Writes on each armed hit, Vblank at each vblank, Scanline whenever LY changes, EveryInstruction after every instruction. The predicate is evaluated once before the first instruction; if it holds, the stop has zero instructions used. Breakpoints (before the instruction) and watches (at the access) win; a predicate stop also defers to a breakpoint at the same boundary.
- Tests in `crates/engine/tests/until.rs` (14 cases) all compare against an independent oracle that steps one instruction at a time and evaluates the same `Condition`: same PC, ticks, instruction count and value. The oracle pinned `u16[wFrame] >= 60` from `Main.loop` at PC $016C, 537 instructions, 13,632 ticks; a width-2 high-byte case ($0100 at $0170) proves both bytes are armed.
- `crates/engine/examples/until_bench.rs`: `cargo run --release -p gbcli-engine --example until_bench -- 10000` (best of 3, 10k iterations, Apple M1, other agents building): restore 20us, floor (537 instr, no predicate) 48us, Writes 136us (87us overhead), EveryInstruction 931us (883us overhead) = 6.9x. Both stop at $016C with 537 instructions.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE APPROVED RULE (design §11 records both)
1. The pure ordering "take the finest trigger" is not exact for a mixed predicate such as `frame >= 3 && u16[wFrame] == 2`: Vblank alone misses a mid-frame write. As built, write candidates stay armed for every cadence except EveryInstruction (which already catches every write), while the reported cadence is the max. `a_mixed_frame_and_memory_predicate_still_stops_on_the_write` pins this.
2. `[rLY] >= 100` is not exactly evaluable: `io_register` returns `Unsupported(SideEffectFreeIo)` at instruction boundaries where SameBoy has batched mode-3 cycles (§2.3). The exact EveryInstruction IO test uses `[rDIV]` (also hardware-updated, always readable); `ly` remains the exact scanline predicate.

RESIDUAL GAP: a raw CPU address in WRAMX or cart RAM (`[$D000]`, `[$A000]`) is armed for the bank mapped at run start; a later bank switch changes that byte without a write to the armed address. A symbol reads in its own bank, and the region form is banked by offset, so both are exact.

TESTS: `cargo test --workspace` green after `python3 -I scripts/corpus/fetch.py --only blargg --only mooneye --only gbmicrotest --only dmg-acid2`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

WORKTREE: /Users/ben/.local/share/opencode/worktree/9786c8/until-cadence, detached HEAD at f101554 (not committed; integrator commits).
Work complete and tests green; handed back for integration. See the leaf note.

Merge-time correction to the cadence rule (integrator, after review). The residual gap the leaf's note recorded is closed:

- Every IO read now takes the every-instruction baseline, not just the five named registers. Internal writes from the serial port, APU and PPU do not pass through the write hook, so no IO register is safe to arm without auditing SameBoy; `[rLCDC]` predicates pay per-instruction, and the design §11 table says so.
- A raw CPU address in any switchable area (cart RAM, WRAMX, ROMX) also takes the baseline. The first build armed cart-RAM/WRAMX addresses for the bank mapped at run start, which a later bank switch invalidates. Symbols and region forms map to a named bank and stay on the cheap path.

Both are exactness fixes: the cheap path is now only where a write to that exact byte is the only way the value changes. `crates/engine/src/cond/cadence.rs` and its unit tests are updated, and design §11's trigger table and residual-gap bullet were corrected in place.

data.title: Refuse save states from before the layer patch, and key the boot cache on core identity
data.description:
Why: the only silent data corruption the review found. Commit 47957a9 grew SameBoy's GB_fifo_item_t from 4 to 6 bytes, so the saved video section is 32 bytes larger. But nothing that identifies the format changed: crates/sameboy/src/blob.rs VERSION is still 2, SameBoy/Core/gb.h STRUCT_VERSION is still 15, and SameBoy/COMMIT is unchanged. SameBoy's read_section (save_state.c:924-944) accepts a smaller saved section and memcpys it, so every field after bg_fifo shifts.

A reviewer ran it: a mid-frame state of layers.gb saved by 47957a9^ loads on HEAD (168,070 vs 168,102 bytes) and its PC diverges from a native run within 1-3 frames. The checkpoint's core-commit field matches, so not even the OtherCommit warning fires. The boot cache key (crates/bundle/src/store.rs:278-287: ROM, model, boot ROM, seed) has no core identity either, so an existing .gbcli/cache/boot-*.gbck is reused.

What: a state from before the patch is refused with a clear error and remedy, never loaded. The core identity a checkpoint records includes the patch set, so a future patch that changes the layout is refused the same way without anyone remembering to bump a number. The boot cache is keyed on that identity, so a stale cache entry is rebuilt rather than reused. Prefer one mechanism that covers future patches (e.g. a hash of patches/ folded into the reported core version at build time) over a hand-bumped constant alone, but bump blob::VERSION now regardless.

Docs, corrected in place as marked block quotes (house rule: a wrong documented cause is worse than none): project/2026-11-06-handoff.md says pre-patch checkpoints "are rejected by the core with a mismatch message"; project/2026-11-06-sameboy-vendoring.md (display.h bullet) says the envelope's core-commit field "already rules out" incompatibility. Both are false.

Seams: crates/sameboy/src/blob.rs, crates/sameboy-sys (build.rs or the COMMIT/version accessor), crates/bundle/src/store.rs (boot-cache key only — the store leaf owns the rest of that file; coordinate if it is in flight). Out of scope: layer capture behavior (its own leaf).

data.title: Layer capture correctness after load, Rendering::Off and repeat vblanks, with tests for the hard cases
data.description:
Why: per-pixel layer identity (47957a9) is right on the paths its tests exercise, but the review found stale or misleading maps on paths they don't, and the tests miss every hard priority case.

Defects (crates/sameboy unless noted):
- Restoring a checkpoint mid-frame with capture on: load (lib.rs:413-458) restores the screen but leaves hooks.layers and layers_skip_next alone, so the next vblank publishes rows from the pre-load timeline. Confirmed by a run: all 64 of object 0's pixels tagged Background. The Core trait doc implies the next frame's map is good.
- With Rendering::Off, supports(PixelLayers) says Yes and set_pixel_layers(true) succeeds, but on_vblank returns before the layers block (hooks.rs:162), so pixel_layers() always errors, blaming LCD-off. Either refuse up front or make it work.
- set_pixel_layers(true) while already on throws away the current valid map (lib.rs:310-316); it should be idempotent.
- Plausible: a CGB GB_VBLANK_TYPE_REPEAT vblank returns before the buffer is refilled (hooks.rs:162-164), so untagged pixels in the next frame inherit old tags rather than the documented "background". Also plausible: on DMG, STOP with the LCD on blacks the screen at a normal vblank (display.c:232-235), and a map is published for a black screen. Confirm each with a test and fix, or show it can't happen.
- The DMG window pixel-insertion glitch pixel (display.c:681-684, 1111-1115) is tagged Background because the inserted item is {0}. Your call whether Window is truer; record it in the vendoring doc.

Typing and docs:
- The tag encoding (0 / 1 / 2+n) is magic numbers in display.c and in hooks.rs layer(). Name it once in C (a define or enum in the patch, shared through the shim) and decode it into the Rust enum in one place.
- Revert the patch's needless change to display.h:33 (a no-break space replaced in an upstream comment), so the patch is smaller to rebase.
- Fix gb.h:679 "one byte per 160-pixel row": it is one byte per pixel, in rows of 160.
- save() clones frame.layers (46 KB) into a Blob that never encodes it (lib.rs:407).
- The vendoring doc's "+0.44% off" figure came from a modified sb_bench.c (CLOCK_PROCESS_CPUTIME_ID) that is not in scripts/. Its claim that "with the buffer NULL the only cost is one branch" ignores the 6-byte FIFO items and render_line's wider object buffer; correct that too.

Tests (crates/sameboy/tests/layers.rs, with layers.asm extended or a second ROM built by scripts/build-roms.sh):
- CGB: LCDC.0 as master priority, the attribute priority bit, and index-based object priority.
- Which object wins where two overlap (the dmg-acid2 check accepts any opaque object pixel, so a wrong index passes).
- LCDC.1 off; a BG-priority object over BG color 0 (the object wins); a mid-frame load; mid-line window disable.

data.title: Make --until cadence sound against bank, LCD-off and same-instruction hits
data.description:
Why: c5da0fe and design §11 claim the cheap write cadence is exact ("Symbols and region forms stay on the cheap path and are exact"; "6.9x faster, and exact"). The review refuted that with four misses, three of them run against a per-instruction oracle. A late or missed --until stop is a silent wrong answer, the worst failure this tool has.

The misses:
1. A WRAM symbol at $D000+ with bank 00 (a DMG game linked with rgblink -w) is armed as BankSel::Bank(0) (cadence.rs:117). The write hook reports gb->cgb_ram_bank, which SameBoy never sets to 0 (memory.c:1651-1653, gb.c:1724), while the evaluator reads bank.max(1) (mem.rs:56). The stop is never reached.
2. A predicate reading both frame and ly: join takes max(), treating Scanline as finer than Vblank (cadence.rs:34, 42-43), and drive.rs:278 never looks at used.frames. With the LCD off, frame advances while LY stays 0, so `frame >= 3 && ly == 0` never stops. With it on, the stop is one scanline late at LY 144. The cadence is really a set of triggers, not a total order.
3. A read hit masks a write in the same instruction. crates/sameboy/src/watch.rs:154-158 records the first hit per instruction, and the until path needs access == Write (drive.rs:273). With a false read watch on $C000, `inc [hl]` records the read and drops the write, so `[$C000] == 5` never stops. Write watches can already be masked the same way.
4. Cart RAM aliasing: the real offset is masked by mbc_ram_size - 1, but the hook reports the raw mbc_ram_bank and address (gbcli_shim.c:42-47, 80). An 8 KB cart with RAMB=1 writing $A000 changes bank 0's byte without matching the bank-0 candidate. Likewise a 2 KB cart at $A800. Plausibly MBC2's mirrored 512 bytes and the Game Boy Camera's capture too.

The root cause of 1 and 4: region_candidate and banked_candidate hand-invert mem::banked_target, with magic $C000/$D000/$A000 constants. Derive the candidates from the same mapping the evaluator reads through, or canonicalize both sides to one (area, bank, offset) identity, so they cannot drift. Where a mapping can't be made exact (Camera capture, MBC quirks), fall back to every-instruction rather than guessing.

Docs: correct design §11's "exact" claims in place, and the trigger table that lists sram:/rom: in two rows. A marked correction block was added at review time pointing here; replace it with the as-built truth.

Tests: extend crates/engine/tests/until.rs's oracle (it is independent, sharing only the evaluator, which is fine) to bank-switched ROMX and SRAM, a -w build's WRAMX symbols, CGB WRAMX via SVBK, small SRAM aliasing, LCD off, mixed frame+ly, and read-watch/write interplay. Each case is red before its fix.

Seams: crates/engine/src/cond/cadence.rs, mem.rs, crates/engine/src/debug/drive.rs (the trigger loop), crates/sameboy/src/watch.rs, crates/sameboy-sys/shim. Out of scope: uninitialized-read semantics and drive.rs tidying (the untilsem leaf, after this one).

criteria.label: Each of the four misses has an oracle test that fails before and passes after (WRAMX bank-0 symbol, frame+ly with LCD off and on, inc [hl] under a read watch, aliased small cart RAM)
Write candidates are derived from the evaluator's own memory mapping (no second hand-written map); a test or type makes drift impossible
Design §11 states the cadence rule as built, with no claim the oracle doesn't back
until_bench re-run, and the cost figure in §11 updated with its command

data.title: --until semantics: unwritten bytes mean "not yet", error stop records, and drive.rs tidying
data.description:
Why: today a predicate reading never-written memory fails the run at once, even from boot, and its remedy says "run from boot". So `run --until 'u16[wFrame] >= 60'` fails on a fresh session, the most natural first use. Mid-run, `[wA]==1 && [wB]==2` fails at the first write to wB if wA is still unwritten.

Already decided (design §8 ruling, 2026-11-06): a condition that triggers a stop (--until, breakpoint or watch --if) reads an unwritten byte as "not yet". At that boundary the whole condition does not hold, without an error, and the cadence keeps waiting on writes. If the run ends without the condition holding while a byte it reads is still unwritten, the stop record carries a warning naming the byte, the symbol and the §8 remedy. Value reads (--read, check, show) keep the uninitialized_read error. --allow-uninit keeps its meaning (read the power-on value). Not per-subexpression: never treat the byte as 0.

Also in this leaf:
- DebugError::Until's stop record says reason: predicate even though the predicate never held (both Until error sites in drive.rs). It should carry the true reason.
- DebugError::UntilSyntax has no test; neither does a mid-run DebugError::Until.
- After a passed-over exec candidate, the core stops before PC X and the loop calls decide on the same hit again (drive.rs:175-208). That evaluates the condition twice and duplicates --allow-uninit warnings. The exec-filter fix in 3b49997 is otherwise correct, and it also fixed a breakpoint on a 4,096-instruction chunk boundary that no test pins; add that test.
- Condition::cadence() and write_candidates() each run cadence::analyze; until.rs:23-33 should analyze once.
- Stale comments: until.rs:17-19 ("a finer cadence leaves this empty" — only EveryInstruction does); a dangling doc link on write_candidates in cond/mod.rs.
- drive.rs is 495 lines; move the fired/until logic into until.rs to get under ~400.
- until_bench's doc says the default is 2,000 iterations; the design cites 10,000. Make them agree.
- Remove the junk `let _ = &mut config;` in the exec-filter regression test (tests/debugger.rs).

Seams: crates/engine/src/cond/, crates/engine/src/debug/. The server's stop_of (handle.rs) not matching DebugError::Until is the server-state leaf's.

data.title: Address grammar: overflow, region bounds, hex bank prefix, symbol offsets
data.description:
Why: crates/engine/src/addr.rs (3b49997) can panic the server, and it silently accepts addresses that don't exist.

- addr.rs:225-227: hram:0x80, io:0x100 and oam:0x200 overflow u16 (a panic in debug builds, kills serve; in release the address wraps to $0000).
- Region offsets are never range-checked: oam:0xA0 gives $FEA0, vram:0x4000 gives bank 2, and wram:0x8000 gives bank 8, on models that lack those banks. Each region's size depends on the model and cart; the error should name the region's real size.
- 0x03:0x4123 is rejected because the region-detection rule (addr.rs:96-98) treats 0x03 as a region name; $03:$4123 works. Design §7 says the prefix is optional in both parts.
- split_offset turns Main+$10000 into Main by falling back to 0. There is no - offset, though the condition language accepts symbol minus a constant.

Every error names the thing, says what happened and gives a corrected form (project/agents/cli-design.md). Seams: addr.rs only; the condition language's own address parsing is in cond/ — if the two duplicate a rule, share it rather than fixing both. Out of scope: poke's bank handling (server-writes leaf).

0x03:0x4123, $03:$4123 and 03:4123 parse identically (test)
Symbol plus or minus an offset either resolves exactly or errors; an overflowing offset errors (test)

data.title: Split server/src/handle.rs into modules (no behavior change)
data.description:
Why: handle.rs is 1,360 lines, three times the house ceiling. Five fix leaves touch it, and in one file they would collide (delegation.md: pre-carve the shared seam in one serial commit, then fan out).

What: a pure move. No behavior change: the existing tests pass unchanged, and no test is edited except for its module path. A suggested split (your call where the boundaries fall):
- handle/mod.rs: Handler, session_request, dispatch, machine_for, warm, log
- run.rs: run, step, after_run_error, budget_of, watch_wall
- config.rs: break, watch, delete
- history.rs: checkpoint, restore, undo, checkpoint_frame
- writes.rs: apply_writes, rom_offset
- reads.rs: show, read, read_values, since
- bundle_ops.rs: sessions, gaps, prune, rm

Each module keeps its tests beside it.
