The test suite passes with no test changed except module paths (state the diff stat of tests)

data.title: Bundle error codes: one mapping from engine errors, no wildcards, distinct variants
data.description:
Why: crates/bundle/src/error.rs (3b49997) gives several failures the wrong code, exit code and remedy, and contradicts both the engine's documented mapping (crates/engine/src/checkpoint_error.rs:72-99) and design §5-6.

checkpoint_code (error.rs:166-175):

| Variant | Mapped to | Should be |
|---|---|---|
| ModelConflict | checkpoint_mismatch, exit 4 | bad_request, exit 2 (§6 step 3) |
| SymbolsMissing | checkpoint_unreadable (via the _ wildcard) | rom_changed |
| PatchConflict | checkpoint_unreadable | rom_changed |
| PatchRefused | checkpoint_unreadable | checkpoint_mismatch |
| Unknown | checkpoint_unreadable | bad_request |

For example, a user who rebuilds without a .sym gets exit 4 and "recreate the checkpoint" instead of "rebuild with -n game.sym, or pass --allow-rom-change".

checkpoint_remedy (error.rs:177-203) re-implements CheckpointError::remedy() instead of calling it: a twin that has already drifted. Use the engine's code and remedy, and match without a wildcard, so a new variant fails to compile rather than mapping silently.

Other mappings:
- Io maps to refused, which the design reserves for "needs a flag", so disk-full shows as an exit-2 usage error. Find or add the right code.
- Configuration covers several unrelated failures, all reported as bad_request with the remedy "check the session's model and seed": an unparseable session.json (store.rs:312), "session already exists" (:125), and "the boot ROM didn't reach the handoff" (:267, which also hides the run's real code). Split it into named variants, each with its own code and remedy.
- SetupError::Core maps to checkpoint_mismatch (error.rs:207), but it is the core refusing a ROM.

Also, in protocol: ErrorCode's hand-written Display (protocol/src/error.rs:102-128) twins the serde spelling. Derive one from the other, or test them together.

Seams: crates/bundle/src/error.rs, crates/protocol/src/error.rs. The store leaf comes after and will use the new variants; keep store.rs edits to the call sites only.

criteria.label: A test per CheckpointError variant asserts its ErrorCode, exit code and remedy through the bundle, and the match has no wildcard arm
Io, an unparseable session.json, an existing session, a failed boot and a core ROM refusal each have a distinct, tested code and remedy
ErrorCode's Display and serde spellings cannot disagree (derived, or one test over every variant)

data.title: Bundle store: session lifecycle, locking, crash consistency and file split
data.description:
Why: crates/bundle/src/store.rs (3b49997) can brick a session, race a deletion against a writer, and corrupt history after a crash. At 854 lines it is also twice the house ceiling.

Lifecycle and locking:
- lock() runs create_dir_all before read_meta (store.rs:460-465), and the server locks first, so one request with a mistyped session name leaves sessions/<name>/lock with no session.json. After that, exists() is true, so serve --rom skips creation and create() refuses; every request fails no_session, and the remedy lists the broken name. Bundle::prune (bundle.rs:143) then fails on the missing session.json, so every prune fails until someone deletes the directory by hand. Locking must never create a session, and prune must survive a broken directory.
- remove() (store.rs:420-430, called by rm and prune) deletes without the session lock. A process mid-run then recreates the session through atomic_write's create_dir_all, and unlinking the lock file lets two writers lock different inodes at once. Take the lock to remove, and keep the lock file outside the directory being removed (or otherwise make this race impossible).
- Prune calls remove(true), which silently deletes sessions that hold named checkpoints, although rm refuses to. It also judges idleness by session.json's mtime, which only head and debugger edits touch, so a session used only for show, read or events looks idle. Record last use explicitly.
- parse_duration (bundle.rs:198-212): split_at(len-1) panics on a non-ASCII last character ("7é" kills serve), and n*60*60*24 is unchecked. In release, "213503982334602d" wraps to about 17 h and prunes everything idle that long. Use checked arithmetic and char-aware parsing.
- Session creation is decided in the CLI adapter (crates/gbcli/src/main.rs:92-114: create when --rom is given and the session is missing, with default model and seed), which also silently ignores --rom when the session exists with a different ROM. Move that decision into the library, and refuse (or explicitly allow) a mismatched ROM with a remedy.

Integrity:
- write_head (store.rs:336-343) writes the head, then the server writes session.json. A kill between them leaves head = N+1 with meta = N. The next save then copies that orphaned head to history/sN, overwriting the real sN. Make the pair crash-consistent; e.g. record the rev in the head file, or write history from meta's rev.
- There is no fsync of file or directory, and a failed rename leaves a .tmp.<pid> file. Decide whether power-loss safety is in scope (state the choice in the design doc), and clean up temp files either way.

Paths and names:
- create() joins a relative ROM path to the project directory but uses a relative .sym as given (relative to cwd) (store.rs:129 vs 134-140), and the .sym error reports a path it did not read (:592). Resolve both the same way.
- checkpoint() (store.rs:346) doesn't validate the name on read, so restore "../history/s3", or an absolute path, reads any .gbck. Use validate_checkpoint_name.
- The CheckpointMissing remedy for ~N lists raw filenames sorted lexically ("s1.gbck, s10.gbck, s2.gbck"); show ~N forms in order.
- validate_name accepts names starting with "-", which a CLI will read as flags.
- Under GBCLI_DIR, project() is the directory's parent whatever it's called; document it, or make it explicit.
- The boot cache shares symbols_live across sessions with different .sym files; key or strip accordingly.

Split store.rs (history, checkpoints, boot cache, io helpers) to get under ~400 lines.

Tests: the bundle.rs walk-up test breaks when GBCLI_DIR is set in the environment; isolate it. Add tests for GBCLI_DIR discovery, the boot-cache key, reuse and corrupt-cache fallback, and ~0 and ~N past the eight kept.

Seams: crates/bundle (all), crates/gbcli/src/main.rs (creation moves out). The event log (events(), log.rs) is the eventlog leaf's; the boot-cache core-identity key is sbver's (landed first).

criteria.label: Tests: a request naming a missing session leaves no trace on disk; prune succeeds with a broken session directory present
Tests: rm and prune take the session lock (a held lock makes them wait, then session_busy); prune skips sessions with named checkpoints or reports them
parse_duration rejects non-ASCII and overflowing input with an error (tests)
A test simulates a kill between the head and meta writes and shows history is not overwritten
Relative ROM and .sym paths resolve against the same base (test); checkpoint names are validated on read (test)
Session creation from --rom lives in the library; gbcli main.rs only wires it
No file in crates/bundle/src over ~400 lines

data.title: Server session state: undo walk-back, once-watches, first-run boot, rev and flag plumbing
data.description:
Why: the server (3b49997) gets session state wrong in ways an agent would act on. The reviewer confirmed most of these by running them.

- Undo toggles (handle.rs:694-730 with store write_head): it always restores ~1, and the replaced head goes to history as rev-1, so a second undo restores what the first replaced. Three 1-frame runs and three undos give frames 2, 3, 2. Already decided (design §10 ruling, 2026-11-06): consecutive undos walk back through history; any other head change resets the walk; undo past the oldest kept entry is refused with a remedy naming the oldest; redo is out of scope.
- --once watches never go away: run and step don't copy machine.debugger_config() back into meta.debugger (only break, watch and delete do: handle.rs:561, 596, 626), so machine_for restores the watch from session.json on the next request. Confirmed: two runs both stop on watchpoint #1.
- write, restore, undo and checkpoint take their machine with Need::Read, which with no head is a power-on machine. So `poke` before the first run saves a power-on head, every later run starts inside the boot ROM, and the boot cache is skipped. checkpoint at rev 0 writes a power-on checkpoint. They should start where run would (the boot cache).
- run --allow-rom-change is ignored: machine_for passes LoadOptions::default(), and only restore reads the flag.
- run --checkpoint records meta.rev before save_head bumps it (the response says s1 but checkpoint.rev is s0).
- stop_of (HEAD handle.rs:836) matches DebugError::Eval but not the newer DebugError::Until, so an --until failure returns a stop record without saving the head that record describes. The reported stop and the head then disagree.
- The warm machine is keyed on session name and rev only (handle.rs:288-294). If another process removes and recreates the session and runs it to the same rev, the warm machine is reused, even with a different ROM. rm never clears self.warm. Key it on something a recreate changes.
- step saves the head with actor None, losing the actor. restore and undo drop load warnings (undo drops all of them). Poke-to-ROM's specific remedy is replaced by a generic core_error remedy.
- The two-process test asserts only rev, which comes from meta; it would pass with a stale warm machine. Compare PC or ticks.

Seams: the split handle modules (history, config, run, mod). Out of scope: run robustness (serverrun), the event log (eventlog), typing (protocol).

criteria.label: Tests: three runs then three undos walk back three states; undo past the oldest kept entry is refused with a remedy; a run after an undo resets the walk
Test: a --once watch fires once across two run requests and is gone from session.json
Test: poke before the first run, then run, starts from the boot cache (since: boot)
Tests: run --allow-rom-change after a rebuild loads; run --checkpoint records the new rev; an --until failure saves the head its stop record describes
Test: rm and recreate at the same rev does not reuse the warm machine; the two-process test compares PC or ticks

data.title: Server run robustness: validate before emulating, wall guard, serve loop, the budget ruling
data.description:
Why: several failures in the run path throw away work or kill serve, and the budget answer contradicts the design's "no answer is exit 3".

- read_values hardcodes allow_uninit: false (handle.rs:939). It runs after the emulation, and a failure returns before save_head, so `run --frames 1 --allow-uninit --read [$C100]` errors, the rev stays the same, there is no stop record, and up to 60 s of emulation is lost. A bad --read expression and an invalid --checkpoint name have the same ordering problem (the name is validated after the run, handle.rs:389-391). Validate and compile everything before emulating; honor --allow-uninit; never discard a completed run because a post-read failed (save the head and report the read error with the stop record).
- The wall guard (watch_wall, handle.rs:844) spawns a thread that sleeps 60 s and is never cancelled, on every run and step. A harness stepping at about 1 kHz holds about 60k sleeping threads until thread::spawn panics. Use one cancellable watchdog. Also: step never rewrites the reason to WallGuard (it reports user_break), and read, restore and boot-cache creation have no guard, though design §3 says the guard backs every request. Make the duration injectable so a test can fire it.
- serve (serve.rs:17-18) ends on one non-UTF-8 byte (lines() plus `line?` gives InvalidData), and nothing catches a panic. A bad line gets a bad_request response and the loop continues. A panic in one request becomes an internal error response, not a dead server; state in the design doc what state is trusted after one (e.g. drop the warm machine).
- Already decided (design §3 ruling, 2026-11-06): a run with a target (--to, --until) whose budget ends first is budget_exhausted, exit 3, explicit budget or not. Reaching the budget is the answer only without a target. Today `run --to X --frames N` that never reaches X returns ok, exit 0 (handle.rs:415-419).
- Magic numbers: Budget::instructions(100_000) (handle.rs:496), events(Some(20)), and a "60 s" in a message that duplicates WALL_GUARD. Name them. Remove `let _ = flag;` (handle.rs:505).

Seams: the split run and reads modules, crates/server/src/serve.rs. Out of scope: the protocol shape of errors (protocol leaf).

criteria.label: Tests: run --allow-uninit --read on unwritten memory succeeds with a warning; a bad --read expression or --checkpoint name fails before any emulation (the rev unchanged, no ticks spent)
Tests: the wall guard fires on run and step with an injected duration, both reporting wall_guard; a thousand step requests leave no lingering threads
Tests over serve's stdio: a non-UTF-8 line gets bad_request and the next line is answered; an injected panic gets an error response and the loop continues
Test: run --to X --frames N that doesn't reach X is budget_exhausted, exit 3; run --frames N alone is ok

data.title: Event log and gap ledger: args, rotation, the right writer, every Unsupported
data.description:
Why: design §10 makes events.jsonl the audit trail and the gap ledger the record of every unsupported feature an agent hit. As built (3b49997) both are incomplete, and rev_mismatch blames the wrong actor.

- EventLogLine (protocol/src/session.rs:55-72) records the op name but not its args; §10 requires "the op and its args". Use the typed Op, not a String.
- No rotation at 10 MB (§10), and events() (store.rs:507-526) reads and parses the whole file, including on every rev_mismatch. Read the tail.
- rev_mismatch's "changed by" (handle.rs:216-221) takes the newest event with rev_after == meta.rev. Reads, failures and earlier refusals all log rev_after == rev, so a later show by another actor is blamed, and only 20 events are scanned. Match rev_before != rev_after, and don't let readers push the writer out of the scan.
- --allow-rom-change is never logged, though §6 says it is.
- Write-path Unsupported errors go through Failure::new(convert::core_error(..)) (handle.rs:964, 987, 995, 1008) with no gap entry, so an MMM01 --patch is never logged; §10 says every Unsupported is. Failure.gap is (&'static str, &'static str) rather than the typed Feature.
- The per-event gaps map (handle.rs:799-803) holds the whole bundle's counts, but EventLogLine.gaps is documented as this session's.

Seams: crates/protocol/src/session.rs, crates/bundle/src/log.rs and events(), the split handle modules.

criteria.label: Tests: an event line carries the op's args; the log rotates past a size threshold (injectable) and events() still returns the newest
Test: alice writes, bob reads, carol's stale write is told alice
Tests: --allow-rom-change is logged; an Unsupported from a poke or patch lands in the gap ledger; per-event gap counts are this session's

data.title: Protocol typing: enums for from/since, refuse unknown fields, typed gap and op
data.description:
Why: the CLI leaf (LUax7P) is next, and it consumes these types. Fix the stringly typed seams now, or the CLI grows a twin parse of each, which the house rules forbid (one struct across a serialization seam).

- RunArgs.from and since are free strings matched against "boot" and "power-on" in the server (handle.rs:327-337, 750-766). Make them protocol enums.
- Unknown fields are accepted: Request uses #[serde(flatten)] and no args struct sets deny_unknown_fields. So "revv":"s3" silently skips the stale-rev guard, and "args":{"frame":10} silently runs the default budget. Refuse unknown fields with bad_request naming the field and the nearest known one. Check that flatten and deny_unknown_fields work together in serde; they often don't, and the fix may be to restructure rather than flatten.
- Response has ok: bool beside the result and error Options, and ResultBody is a bag of Options, so invalid combinations are representable. Your call how far to go: at least make ok derived from which of the two is present, so it can't disagree.
- BudgetLimits' doc says "null when the caller didn't say", but the fields are omitted. Make the doc and the bytes agree.

Seams: crates/protocol, with the server call sites. Pinned response-byte tests may change; explain each change. Blocks the CLI leaf LUax7P.

criteria.label: from and since are enums in protocol, and the server matches them exhaustively
Tests: a request with an unknown top-level or args field gets bad_request naming it
Response cannot represent ok:true with an error (type or test)

data.title: Re-review the fixes: independent pass over the changed surfaces

data.text:
addr: done in worktree agent-ab490ca902f891f9a (uncommitted). addr.rs became crates/engine/src/addr/{mod,offset,sizes,tests}.rs.

- Region offsets are bounded by RegionSizes (RegionSizes::of(core) reads every CPU-mapped region's length; RegionSizes::ANY_MODEL is the bound without a machine). New AddrError::RegionOffset names the size, the banks, "on this machine"/"on any model", and the last valid offset; sram on a RAM-less cart says so. No more u16 overflow (hram:0x80 etc.).
- Bank-qualified head = any hex (prefixed or not); non-hex head = region. 0x03:0x4123 == $03:$4123 == 03:4123.
- Symbol offsets: + and -, hex. Must stay in $0000-$FFFF, and in the symbol's switchable area when it has a bank; else AddrError::SymbolOffset with the offsets that fit. Labels are written as the grammar reads them (Main+$10); romcheck now splits labels with addr::split_label (its own decimal splitter is gone).
- New API: addr::parse_on / parse_write_on (take &RegionSizes). The server still calls parse/parse_write (ANY_MODEL bound) until it switches: addr::parse_on(text, machine.symbols(), &RegionSizes::of(machine.core())?).
- Criteria: yJj, a3t, l3d all covered by tests in crates/engine/src/addr/tests.rs; RegionSizes::of covered in crates/engine/tests/inspect_regions.rs; label round-trip through romcheck in crates/engine/tests/checkpoints.rs.
- Integration notes (not done; owned elsewhere): cond/parse.rs region() duplicates inspect::regions::parse_region (and spells bootrom "boot", case-sensitive); cond/parse.rs banked_symbol duplicates addr's switchable-area rule; debug/record.rs, debug/backtrace.rs and cond/eval.rs print symbol offsets in decimal (Main.loop+3 fine, Main+16 means $16 to the grammar) — they should call addr::label.

Integration notes from the address-grammar leaf (7GcXJC), for this leaf's surface (cond/, debug/):
- debug/record.rs:33, debug/backtrace.rs:53 and cond/eval.rs:300 print symbol offsets in decimal (Name+16), but the address grammar reads offsets as hex, so a user copying Main+16 from a stop record gets $16. Use addr::label (7GcXJC writes labels as Name+$hex; user approved that format).
- cond/parse.rs region() duplicates inspect::regions::parse_region but is case-sensitive and spells `boot` where everything else uses `bootrom`; call parse_region.
- cond/parse.rs banked_symbol duplicates the switchable-area rule; use addr::offset::banked_area (pub(crate), re-exported from addr by 7GcXJC).

From 7GcXJC: the address grammar now bounds region offsets and banks by the machine's real sizes, but only through addr::parse_on / parse_write_on with &RegionSizes::of(machine.core())?. The server still calls addr::parse / parse_write (largest-any-model bounds), so wram:0x2000 on a DMG still resolves to bank 2. Switch the call sites (were handle.rs:363, 556, 586, 963, 980, 1029 before the split) to the _on forms — belongs with this leaf's poke-bank fix.

addr, follow-up: a bank-qualified address in a bank the machine lacks is now refused (AddrError::BankRange, bad_address), checked against RegionSizes in parse_on/parse_write_on for ROMX, WRAMX, SRAM and VRAM; message names the bank count and range ("4 ROM banks (00-03) on this machine"), remedy gives the last bank at the same address (03:4123); a RAM-less cart says so. ANY_MODEL refuses only ROM >1FF, WRAM >07, cart RAM >0F, VRAM >01. Tests: addr::tests::a_bank_the_machine_lacks_is_refused_naming_the_banks_it_has and without_a_machine_only_banks_past_every_model_are_refused (both red first). Design §7 Update block extended (bank rule, approved label-format caveat). fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --workspace: all pass, 13.8 s warm.

data.text: Split crates/server/src/handle.rs into handle/{mod,run,config,history,writes,reads,bundle_ops,test_support}.rs in worktree agent-ab7a10bdff13d2216 (uncommitted). Pure move; fmt, clippy -D warnings and cargo test --workspace pass (26 s warm). Same 15 handle test names, bodies byte-identical after dedent. Largest file mod.rs 378 lines.

Built in worktree agent-ae3ec99eacf779e55 (branch worktree-agent-ae3ec99eacf779e55), uncommitted.

Design: candidates are now backing bytes, not (CPU address, bank) pairs. The analysis (cond/cadence.rs) resolves each read byte with the evaluator's own mapping (mem::fixed_target / mem::banked_target / region offset) and the core matches writes by the byte they land in (new core::StoreFilter on RunRequest::stores; SameBoy's watch::store_of, shared with never-written tracking, uses the shim's size-masked cart RAM offset). Cart RAM is armed only where the new Feature::CartRamWrites is Yes (no MBC, MBC1/3/5, MMM01); otherwise every-instruction. ROM reads arm nothing (constant).
Triggers are a set (vblank, scanline, every_instruction, stores); the protocol Cadence stays as the label of the costliest one.
StopReason::Candidate now carries Hits (every hit of the instruction, in order); drive.rs decides each in order and any write hit re-evaluates the predicate.

data.title: Cart memory fidelity: unmirrored mappers, MBC1 mode-1 ROM0, aliased cart RAM reads and banked watches
data.description:
Why: the --until cadence leaf (aKvkO5, commit 824af3f) found four cart-memory fidelity gaps outside its scope. Each makes a read, a watch or an uninitialized-read check disagree with hardware on some carts, which is a silent wrong answer.

What, each with a red-first test:
- Never-written tracking never marks cart RAM on MBC2, MBC7, HuC1/3, TPP1 or camera carts (gbcli_cart_ram_offset returns -1 for mappers gbcli_cart_ram_mirrored doesn't cover, in crates/sameboy-sys/shim/gbcli_shim.c), so every cart RAM read there looks uninitialized. Either mirror those paths or report the bytes as untracked rather than unwritten.
- The evaluator reads ROM0 flat (crates/engine/src/mem.rs), ignoring MBC1 mode-1 and MMM01 ROM0 banking.
- A banked cart RAM read past the RAM size (e.g. [$01:$A000] on an 8 KiB cart) errors, where hardware aliases it through the size mask.
- Watches with an explicit bank still match SameBoy's unmasked cart RAM bank (crates/sameboy/src/watch.rs), so a watch on bank 0 misses a write aliased through bank 1. The StoreFilter identity from 824af3f is the likely fix: match banked cart-RAM watches by backing byte too.

Seams: crates/engine/src/mem.rs, crates/sameboy/src/watch.rs, crates/sameboy-sys/shim. Out of scope: --until semantics (WooWP7). Check design §2.3 and §11 for the current rules before changing them.

criteria.label: Each of the four gaps has a test that fails before its fix
Design §2.3 or §11 states the rule as built

data.label: Each of the four misses has an oracle test that fails before and passes after (WRAMX bank-0 symbol, frame+ly with LCD off and on, inc [hl] under a read watch, aliased small cart RAM)
Write candidates are derived from the evaluator's own memory mapping (no second hand-written map); a test or type makes drift impossible
Design §11 states the cadence rule as built, with no claim the oracle doesn't back
until_bench re-run, and the cost figure in §11 updated with its command

data.note: Integrated in 824af3f after reading the core of the diff (shim, watch.rs, filter/stop types, cadence.rs, drive.rs). All four criteria verified: red-first oracle tests per miss, one mapping (mem::fixed_target/banked_target) with StoreFilter identity, §11 rewritten, bench re-run (6.2x). Out-of-scope findings filed as a new leaf under jPKQX8 (cart memory fidelity). Brief corrections from the agent: a write hit never masked the predicate (only a read hit did); the camera does not write cart RAM on capture; [$02:A000] does not lex (address after : must start with $ or a digit) — a cond/parse.rs gap for WooWP7.

data.text: From aKvkO5: in cond/parse.rs, [$02:A000] fails to parse because an address after the colon starting with a letter lexes as an identifier; [$02:$A000] works. The addr grammar (7GcXJC) accepts 02:A000 — make the two agree.

Done in worktree agent-af870380132c54a7a (uncommitted). All three criteria met; fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --workspace pass (24.6 s wall incl. build).

- checkpoint_code: exhaustive, no wildcard, per the engine's documented codes (they agree with design §6). Remedy is CheckpointError::remedy(); the bundle twin is gone. The engine has no CheckpointError::code(), so the code mapping still lives in the bundle — moving it to the engine (like AddrError::code) is a follow-up for whoever owns crates/engine.
- New ErrorCodes: io_failed (exit 5) for Io and NoRoot; session_unreadable (exit 4) for an unparseable session.json. Design §5 has an Update block with the new table; §6 has one with the code per CheckpointError variant.
- Configuration removed; split into SessionExists (bad_request), SessionUnreadable (session_unreadable), BootFailed(DebugError) (refused, or unsupported when the core lacks a feature), BadHistoryRef / BadCheckpointName / BadDuration (bad_request). store.rs and bundle.rs touched at the constructing call sites only.
- SetupError::Core: rom_unreadable, or unsupported for CoreError::Unsupported.
- ErrorCode Display vs serde: one test over every code, with an exhaustive match that won't compile until a new code is listed.
Open: StoreError::CheckpointMissing (checkpoint_unreadable, exit 4) and CheckpointError::Unknown (bad_request, exit 2) are the same failure with two codes. Not changed; it needs a ruling.

From 4GpAGx: crates/server/src/convert.rs:42-43 maps CoreError::InvalidState and CoreError::Backend to `refused`, which the design reserves for "needs a flag". Map them like the bundle now does (io_failed / rom_unreadable / checkpoint_mismatch as fits; see design §5 update from 4GpAGx). Also: a failed boot-cache build surfaces as StoreError::BootFailed → `refused` with remedy --from power-on, because the bundle cannot call the server mapping of run errors; once DebugError has a code() in the engine, the bundle and convert.rs should both use it.

Follow-up per coordinator: CheckpointError::code() now lives in the engine (exhaustive, a test per variant); the bundle calls it and its own match is gone. Ruling applied: StoreError::CheckpointMissing is bad_request (exit 2), remedy still lists known names; checkpoint_unreadable's fallback remedy no longer says "check the checkpoint name". Design §5/§6 Update blocks revised. fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --workspace pass.

data.note:
Maps store errors to the codes the engine and design state, with no wildcard

The bundle's checkpoint mapping disagreed with the engine on five
variants: a --model conflict exited 4 instead of 2, and a rebuild
without a .sym exited 4 with "recreate the checkpoint" instead of
rom_changed. It also kept its own copy of the engine's remedies.
CheckpointError now owns its code as well as its remedy: code() matches
every variant without a wildcard, so a new variant fails to compile
instead of mapping silently, and the bundle passes both through.

Filesystem failures were reported as `refused`, which the design keeps
for "needs a flag", and a damaged session.json as bad_request. The
protocol gains io_failed (exit 5) and session_unreadable (exit 4). The
catch-all Configuration variant is split into named variants, each with
its own code and remedy. A core refusing a ROM is rom_unreadable rather
than checkpoint_mismatch. Naming a checkpoint that doesn't exist is a
caller mistake, so the store reports it as bad_request, as the engine
already did.

ErrorCode's Display and serde spellings are tested together over every
code. Design §5 and §6 have Update blocks with the new exit table and
the per-variant checkpoint codes. The server's convert.rs still maps
InvalidState and Backend to `refused`; that is noted on leaf 45AjcH.

data.label: Tests: --until on unwritten memory from boot runs until the write makes it true; a budget end with a still-unwritten read carries the warning; --read on unwritten memory still errors; a breakpoint --if on unwritten memory does not stop
DebugError::Until's stop record carries the true reason (test); UntilSyntax and mid-run Until each have a test

data.note:
Treats never-written memory in stop triggers as "not yet" and gives --until failures their own reason

Design §8 ruling: `run --until 'u16[wFrame] >= 60'` failed at once from
boot, the most natural first use. A condition that triggers a stop
(--until, breakpoint or watch --if) now evaluates through
Condition::verdict, where a never-written byte makes the whole condition
"not yet": no stop, no error, never read as 0. A run that ends while one
still waits on an unwritten byte warns (in the response's warnings, not
a stop-record field), naming the byte, symbol and remedy. Value reads
keep uninitialized_read; --allow-uninit is unchanged.

DebugError::Until's stop record said `predicate` though the predicate
never held; it is now the new `predicate_error` reason. A passed-over
exec candidate was decided twice; it is now decided once, and a test
pins the chunk-boundary breakpoint the re-check exists for. drive.rs
splits into decide.rs and until.rs (497 -> 264 lines). Symbol offsets
print as the address grammar reads them (Work+$B); condition region
names and bank-qualified addresses match the address grammar, so
`[boot:0]` is now `[bootrom:0]`.

Four existing tests changed because the expected behavior changed: a
breakpoint condition on unwritten memory now waits and warns instead of
failing; the until uninitialized-read test is replaced by unwritten.rs;
backtrace labels are hex; the until oracle uses verdict.

data.note:
Makes the bundle store crash-consistent and safe to lock, remove and prune

The first store could brick a session (locking a mistyped name left a
lock-only directory that made every later request no_session and every
prune fail), race rm against a writer (rm unlinked a lock another
process held), silently prune named checkpoints, judge idleness by

writes overwrite real history. parse_duration panicked on non-ASCII
input and wrapped on overflow.

names them, so an orphaned write is overwritten, never history. Lock
files live in .gbcli/locks/ and are never unlinked; their mtime records
last use; lock() never writes for a missing session; rm, prune and
create take the lock; prune skips sessions with named checkpoints and
survives broken directories. Session creation from --rom moves into
Bundle::open_session, which refuses a mismatched ROM. Relative ROM and

misses list ~0..~8 in order, the boot cache drops symbol fields, and
failed writes clean up their temp files. Power-loss durability is out
of scope (design §1, backlog). store.rs is split into store, session,
history, checkpoints, boot, lock, io and prune modules.

No migration for bundles made by older builds (accepted pre-release). A
relative --rom now resolves against the working directory.

Built in worktree agent-a6dc039db2dd822da (srvchain), uncommitted.

- Undo walk: SessionFile.undo {restored, origin}; SessionStore::undo_target; write_head(cp, rev, walk) keeps history 8 back from the walk's origin so 8 undos are reachable; StoreError::UndoPastOldest (bad_request, remedy names the oldest sN). save_head (now handle/head.rs, HeadChange struct) clears the walk on every other head change.
- Found beyond the brief: a cold handler (fresh serve, any CLI process) answered show/read/break/watch from POWER-ON, never loading the head (Need::Read asked start_machine for Start::PowerOn, which skips the head). The two-process test passed because it checked only rev. Fixed (Need::Head -> SessionStore::head_or_power_on), and the test now compares the machine's frame; red verified by reverting the one line.
- Need is now Head / Start(Start) / Replace. write and checkpoint start where run does (boot cache); restore and undo don't load the head (a rebuilt ROM that makes the head unloadable no longer blocks the restore).
- Warm machine keyed on SessionFile.incarnation (new field, set at create); rm forgets it.
- save_head copies the debugger config (once-watches gone); stop_of matches Until (exhaustive); run --checkpoint after the save; step keeps its actor; undo/restore surface load warnings; addr parse_on/parse_write_on everywhere; bank-qualified poke uses banked_target; poke to ROM is `refused` with design §4's remedy.
- Fixture and gbcli/tests/serve.rs use Bundle::open_or_create_in (now pub); the serve tests env_remove GBCLI_DIR on the child.
- Green on first run: a_run_after_an_undo_resets_the_walk (the old toggle and the new reset give the same answer for that sequence; it guards the reset). restore_over_a_rebuild_does_not_load_the_head_first passed before the fix only because cold reads skipped the head (the bug above).
- Still open (not fixed): a warm machine isn't checked against the ROM file, so a long-lived serve keeps the old ROM across a rebuild until the head moves.

Built (worktree agent-adbd6ff0e67e44393, uncommitted). Rule as built: design §2.3 "Update, 2026-11-06 (leaf fenCqJ)"; §11 table corrected in place.

1. Unmirrored mappers (MBC2, MBC7, HuC1/3, TPP1, camera): chose "untracked", not mirroring. SameBoy's written(Sram) returns Unsupported(CartRamWrites) when gbcli_cart_ram_mirrored is false, so never_written / the uninit check skip their cart RAM. Why: mirroring means tracking write_mbc_ram per mapper (MBC7 EEPROM, HuC3 modes, HuC1 IR + writes with RAM disabled, TPP1 modes, camera registers/busy) through every SameBoy update, for mappers homebrew rarely uses; one shim fact now decides both the feature and tracking. Blob layout unchanged (bits still kept, just not exposed).
2. ROM0 banking: new required trait method Core::rom0_bank() (SameBoy: GB_DIRECT_ACCESS_ROM0). mem::bank_at uses it; banked_target reads ROM0 in its bank; ROM0 by CPU address is now switchable, so its cadence is every_instruction (unit test assertion for [$0100] changed for that reason).
3. Aliasing: mem::target_in_bank / mem::target alias ROM and cart RAM offsets through CartSizes (power-of-two sizes). Region forms (rom:, sram:) are never aliased. banked_target stays unaliased (server patch path).
4. Banked watches: shim cart_ram_bank now masks by RAM size (as rom_bank masks by ROM size), so hits report the reached bank; engine arms explicit ROM/cart RAM banks at mem::effective_bank (breakpoints, watches, --to). Not the StoreFilter route: that is write-only and would need a read-store filter on RunRequest for read watches; masking at the source fixes both.

Shim change does not change the core identity (it hashes patches/, not shim/).

Gaps found, not fixed (no issue-tree root exists, so recorded here):
- Evaluator reads cart ROM at 0000-00FF (0200-08FF CGB) while the boot ROM is mapped (mem.rs ignores rBANK); gbcli_peek handles it.
- Sub-bank cart RAM mirrors (2 KiB at $A800, MBC2 every $200): a watch on $A000 misses a write at $A800. --until is unaffected. Recorded in design §2.3.

data.title: Engine memory map honors the boot ROM overlay
data.description: Found in fenCqJ. crates/engine/src/mem.rs resolves 0000-3FFF to the ROM region (now in the ROM0 bank) whatever the boot ROM mapping: while the boot ROM is mapped (rBANK bit 0 clear), the CPU reads 0000-00FF (and 0200-08FF on CGB) from the boot ROM, but `[$0000]` in a condition, a backtrace or a symbol lookup reads cart ROM. SameBoy's own peek (gbcli_peek) handles this. Fix: resolve those ranges to Region::BootRom while the boot ROM is mapped (io_register(rBANK) or a core accessor); cadence must treat them as switchable (a write to FF50 remaps them). Red-first test: a machine before handoff, `[$0000]` equals the boot ROM's first byte.

data.title: Warm machine notices a rebuilt ROM
data.description: Found by leaf 4xuujC (design §1, its update, "Still open"). The server's warm machine is keyed on session, rev and incarnation, but not on the ROM file: a `serve` that keeps running across an RGBDS rebuild keeps emulating the old ROM until the head moves, while a fresh process sees the rebuild (and the checkpoint ROM check). For the build loop (stage 6) a long-lived serve is the normal case, so this is a silent wrong answer. Fix: key the warm machine on the ROM's identity too (size+mtime cheaply, or the sha the session already records), and when it changed, take the same path a cold load takes (warn/refuse per design §6 and --allow-rom-change). Red test first: serve, run, rewrite the ROM file, run again — the second run must not use the old ROM silently.

data.title: Server re-review fixes: read --allow-uninit, prune/list robustness, defaultable args, save and rm ordering
data.description:
Found by the independent re-review (ZpBFp2, server half; verdict note on jPKQX8). Each with a red-first regression test:
- D3: `read` answers uninitialized_read with the remedy "pass --allow-uninit", but ReadArgs has no allow_uninit (reads.rs passes false). Design §8 says --allow-uninit keeps its meaning for value reads: add it to ReadArgs and honor it.
- D4: prune stops at the first busy session (prune.rs `store.acquire(wait)?`) after removing earlier ones, and answers only session_busy, so the caller thinks nothing was pruned. Skip-and-report busy sessions (or report removed ones with the error); say which in design §1.
- D5: Bundle::list does `self.session(&name)?`, so one stray directory under .gbcli/sessions/ (bad name, or no session.json) turns `sessions` into bad_request; no_session remedies list directories that aren't sessions. List only real sessions; skip (and maybe warn about) the rest, as prune does.
- D6: the undo-past-oldest remedy says "the head is sN, the oldest state kept (8 heads back)" with the oldest entry's rev in the head's slot and a hard-coded distance. Name the head and the oldest kept entry correctly.
- D7: `{"op":"run"}`, `{"op":"step"}`, `{"op":"events"}` and `"args":null` are refused with "missing field `args`" though every field defaults; `{"op":"show","args":{}}` is refused. Accept absent/null/empty args where the op's args are all defaultable (and `{}` for unit ops). A duplicate key inside args (`{"frames":1,"frames":2}`) is accepted, last wins, because args pass through serde_json::Value (parse.rs) — refuse duplicates as the top level does.
- D8: save_head (handle/head.rs) sets meta.rev before write_meta; if that write fails the response and event log report rev N+1 while disk says N. Only bump after a successful write.
- D9: rm (store.rs remove_locked) uses remove_dir_all in readdir order, so a kill midway can leave session.json without its head (HeadMissing until rm again). Remove session.json first, or rename the directory aside, then delete.
- D10: SessionStore::checkpoint maps any read error (EACCES too) to CheckpointMissing (bad_request) instead of io_failed; an Unsupported arriving through a store error (BootFailed(Core(Unsupported)), Setup) goes through Failure::from_store with gap None, so it never reaches the gap ledger.
- Doc: after a run resets the walk, undo walks back through heads earlier undos wrote (frames 1,2,3,2,1 is correct per §10 but surprising): say so in design §10.

data.title: Decide which ops accept --allow-rom-change after a rebuild
data.description: Ruling needed (found by ZpBFp2 server half, D2). After a ROM rebuild, show/read/break/watch/delete/step/write/checkpoint/undo all answer rom_changed with "…or pass --allow-rom-change to load it anyway", but only run and restore accept the flag (design §6 names it for those); undo cannot cross a rebuild at all, and restore takes only named checkpoints, not ~N. Before 4xuujC, cold inspect requests read power-on and hid this. Options: (A, recommended) make allow_rom_change a top-level request field like rev, honored by every op that loads a stored state, so the CLI flag is global and every remedy is true; (B) keep it on run/restore and change every other op's remedy to name the command that works (`run --allow-rom-change --frames 0`?), and let restore take ~N; (C) per-op flags on each state-loading op. Whichever: undo should be able to cross a rebuild with the flag.

data.title: Engine re-review fixes: CGB DMA write redirect, WRAMX bank 0 watches, grammar agreement, identity coverage
data.description:
Found by the independent re-review (ZpBFp2, engine half; verdict note on jPKQX8). Red-first regression test for each confirmed item; probes are in the review's scratchpad file reveng-rev_probe.rs if still present.
1. CONFIRMED: --until misses a write that CGB OAM DMA's bus conflict moves. SameBoy's write callback fires before the redirect (memory.c ~1838-1871): on CGB, while OAM DMA reads a non-WRAM source, a CPU write to WRAM lands at ((src-1)&0x1000)|(addr&0xFFF)|0xC000. The store hit and never-written tracking (crates/sameboy/src/watch.rs ~216-224) use the CPU's address. Scenario: CGB-E, HRAM routine `ld a,$40; ldh [$46],a; ld a,$77; ld [$D123],a`; `run_until "[$C123] == $77"` should stop at the 5th instruction, runs to budget. On DMG the write is dropped, so only tracking is wrong. Fix at the source: report the byte the write actually lands in (shim), so watch hits, store hits and tracking agree; add the case to design §11 and correct cadence.rs's "cannot disagree" claim if it stays untrue anywhere.
2. CONFIRMED: a watch or breakpoint on WRAMX bank 00 (`00:D000`, an rgblink -w symbol, or CGB SVBK 0) never fires: mem::effective_bank aliases only ROM and SRAM, the shim reports cgb_ram_bank (never 0), while the evaluator already reads bank 0 as 1 (mem.rs ~179). Alias WRAMX bank 0 to 1 in effective_bank (and check VRAM/other areas for the same shape).
3. CONFIRMED, low: conditions and the address grammar disagree: `[ff:4000]`/`[A:4000]` are "isn't a region" in conditions (cond/parse.rs ~181-195) while the grammar accepts `ff:4000`; and register+offset radix differs (`rLCDC+10` is $FF4A in conditions, $FF50 in the grammar; `_AUD3WAVERAM+16` reaches rDMA). Make both grammars resolve these the same way and state the one rule in design §7/§8.
4. PLAUSIBLE: the core identity hashes crates/sameboy-sys/patches/, not the compiled pre-patched SameBoy/Core tree; an edit made directly in SameBoy/Core without regenerating the patch keeps PATCH_SET and loads a changed layout silently. Add a check (test or build-time) that patches/ matches what is applied in SameBoy/Core, or hash what is compiled; update the vendoring doc.
5. PLAUSIBLE, low: the evaluator reads cart RAM bytes where the CPU reads an MBC3 RTC register or $FF (RAM disabled). Make [$A000] return what the CPU would read, or report it as not side-effect-free readable; at least document.
6. PLAUSIBLE, low: hits past Hits::CAPACITY (8) in one step (CGB GDMA reads its source via GB_read_memory) are dropped for watches; `overflowed` is only honored for --until. A read watch on source byte 9+ is silently missed. Fall back (e.g. re-decide by stepping) or grow the buffer.

data.title: Fix: a STOPped SameBoy core never wakes on set_keys (stale JOYP in gbcli_pre_run)
data.description:
A core in STOP never wakes on a key pressed while it is stopped.

`gbcli_pre_run` (crates/sameboy-sys/shim/gbcli_shim.c:276) returns GBCLI_PRE_STOPPED when `gb->stopped` and JOYP's low nibble reads $F, and `run` (crates/sameboy/src/run.rs:100) then stops with StopReason::Stopped before calling GB_run. But `set_keys` -> GB_set_key_mask only sets `gb->keys` and `inputs_changed`; SameBoy recomputes JOYP's low nibble in GB_joypad_run (joypad.c:212), which only runs inside GB_run. So the check reads a stale JOYP and the core can never be woken by Core::set_keys + Core::run.

Observed 2026-11-06 (leaf 5ewkYZ, scratch test): docboy/cpu/interactive/stop_joypad0_interrupt0.gb from docboy's hand-over: run -> Stopped at 8,464 ticks; set_keys(UP) -> JOYP still $EF; run -> Stopped again. A P1 write that changes the select bits (which calls GB_update_joyp, memory.c:1592-1625) makes the next run proceed (Budget). This one bug accounts for 19 docboy failures ("the CPU stopped with no wake source": stop_read_ly*, stop_read_stat*, stop_read_tima*, stop_tima_falling_edge, stop_joypad0_interrupt*, dma_stop_during_transfer_timing*, stop_trigger_interrupt, stop_hello_world, mbc3_rtc_gb_stopped_recover). See project/2026-11-06-docboy-baseline.md.

Fix at the source: make the STOP check see the current keys (e.g. have the shim refresh JOYP before checking, or apply the key mask's effect on JOYP in set_keys), with a red-first test in crates/sameboy (tests/roms/stop.asm exists). Then re-run `cargo run --release -p gbcli-corpus -- --check tests/corpus/baseline-sameboy.json` and rewrite the baseline: those rows should flip.

1. CGB OAM-DMA write redirect: FIXED at the source. New shim accessor gbcli_write_target mirrors GB_write_memory's bus-conflict redirect (plus SameBoy's static is_addr_in_dma_use/bus_for_addr); watch.rs on_write matches, records and tracks the landing address; a dropped write is no write. Red tests: until/banks.rs a_cpu_write_that_cgb_oam_dma_moves_stops_where_it_lands (oracle), watch_targets.rs a_write_cgb_oam_dma_moves_is_watched_where_it_lands, a_write_dmg_oam_dma_drops_leaves_its_byte_unwritten. Rule: a write watch fires on the byte that changes. cadence.rs claim corrected.
2. WRAMX bank 00: FIXED. mem::effective_bank aliases WramX bank 0 -> 1. Red tests: watch_targets.rs a_watch_on_wramx_bank_00_fires, a_breakpoint_on_wramx_bank_00_fires. VRAM needs no alias.
3. Grammar: bank head FIXED (hex head is a bank in conditions too: [ff:4000], [A:4000]); red test cond::tests::a_bank_head_that_is_all_hex_letters_is_a_bank_as_in_the_address_grammar. Offset radix NOT FIXED: needs a product decision. Confirmed by probe: grammar rLCDC+10 = $FF50, condition [rLCDC+10] = $FF4A; _AUD3WAVERAM+16 = $FF46 vs $FF40; symbol offsets (Main+10) differ the same way. Hex-in-conditions makes a literal's radix context-dependent and contradicts §8 decimal integers; decimal-in-grammar (RGBDS/hardware.inc convention, matches old decimal checkpoint labels) changes §7's documented `rLCDC+10 is $FF50` and 7GcXJC's "hex, prefixed or not". Recommendation: decimal everywhere, `$`/`0x` for hex (labels already print `+$B`, so they round-trip). Design §7 records the disagreement (marked correction) and the open question. Criterion Zag left pending for this.
4. Core identity: test added. SameBoy/CORE_SHA256 records upstream Core's hash (scripts/sameboy-core-hash.sh); tests/patch_set.rs reverse-applies patches/ to a copy and requires that hash. Value verified against GitHub's tarball of ea667ad; a direct edit to Core/timing.c made the test fail. vendor-sameboy.sh writes the file. Identity computation unchanged; no states refused.
5. Cart RAM CPU-address reads: DOCUMENTED (design §2.3 update) — reads the cart RAM byte of the selected bank even when disabled/RTC-mapped; reasons given. Note: SameBoy returns open bus (data_bus) for disabled RAM, not $FF as the leaf says.
6. Hits past capacity: FIXED. Hits is a first hit + Vec (no alloc for one hit), no CAPACITY/overflowed; Stop/StopReason lose Copy (server and corpus compile unchanged). Red test: watch_targets.rs every_watched_read_of_a_cgb_gdma_is_seen.

Suite: cargo fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --workspace all pass (536 tests). Wall time 124 s at load average ~190 (other agents), not a meaningful warm figure; new tests add ~0.2 s.

data.label: Items 4–6 fixed with a test, or documented with the reason in the design or vendoring doc

data.title: Decide one radix for offsets after a name in both grammars
data.description: Ruling needed (found by TCSC3C, item 3). The two grammars read an offset after a name in different radixes: the address grammar (design §7, leaf 7GcXJC: "hex, prefixed or not") reads `rLCDC+10` as $FF50 and `Main+10` as Main+$10; conditions (§8: integers are decimal unless $/0x/%) read `[rLCDC+10]` as $FF4A and `[Main+10]` as Main+10. hardware.inc's `_AUD3WAVERAM+10` names are decimal and match whole first. Either single rule changes a documented meaning. Options: (A, agent's recommendation) decimal everywhere, `$`/`0x` for hex — as RGBDS and hardware.inc read offsets; labels already print as `Main+$B`, so they read back right; old checkpoints' decimal labels like `Main+16` read correctly again. Changes §7's "rLCDC+10 is $FF50". (B) hex after a name in both — a number's radix would depend on what it's added to, against §8. (C) refuse a bare number after a name in both, requiring `$10` or `#16`-style explicit radix.

criteria.label: User ruling recorded in design §7 and §8, and both grammars follow it (test)

A warm machine is reused only when a cold load with the request's own options would build the same machine:

data.title: Wire screenshots and views into the server and protocol
data.description: The server/CLI half of qliE6W. The library (crates/view, commit with this leaf's found-in) renders labeled frames, crops, scales, filmstrips, diffs and tileset/tilemap/OAM PNGs; the wiring spec is design §9's qliE6W update. In short: RunArgs.shot {path, scale, crop, live, any_frame}; after the reads (§11 step 6): capture → cropped → scaled → png → write; the result carries shot {path, width, height, scale, frame}. NotNormal maps to exit 1 with a hint to pass --any-frame. FrameSource::Complete's frame counts from power-on and must be rebased to the session's time base as frame_shown is (engine/debug/record.rs). FrameSource needs a protocol wire type (view has no serde) — one struct both sides import. `view tiles|map|oam` returns inspect::video data first, the PNG on request. Filmstrips need the run loop to collect frames. A screenshot never advances emulation (the library has a state test; keep one at the server level).

data.title: Palette-RAM pokes reach frames on CGB
data.description: Found by qliE6W (see project/gotchas.md, 2026-11-06 "poking CGB palette RAM doesn't change what SameBoy draws"). poke(Region::BgPalette/ObjPalette) changes palette RAM, but SameBoy renders from its converted-color cache (background_palettes_rgb, object_palettes_rgb), which only BCPD/OCPD writes refresh (GB_palette_changed). So inspection and the tilemap view show the poked color while frames don't: a silent disagreement. Fix at the source: after a palette poke, refresh the cache (a shim accessor calling GB_palette_changed per entry, or the backend's poke path doing so). Red-first test: poke a CGB palette entry, run one frame, the frame pixel shows the new color. Then delete the gotcha entry.

criteria.label: Test: a poked CGB palette color appears in the next frame; the gotcha entry is removed

Then delete the gotcha entry.

data.title: Key input on run: a --keys timeline (design §11 step 3)
data.description:
Why: no request can press a button yet. The engine has Machine::set_keys and the core wakes from STOP on input (Jwo9sg), but RunArgs carries no input, so an agent can't drive a game: "make a sprite move" is untestable through the CLI or the server.

What (design §11 step 3): RunArgs gains a key timeline, `--keys 'A@0 -A@2 START@10'` on the CLI (press at a frame offset, `-` releases), and `--keys-file <file>` for long scripts (design §12: bodies come from files). Offsets count frames from the run's start. The engine applies each event at the vblank where its frame begins; held keys persist in the head (they already round-trip through the checkpoint header's `keys`). Parse errors name the token and show the grammar. A key event past the run's stop is reported, never silently dropped.

criteria.label: A run with --keys presses and releases on the stated frames, checked by a test ROM that records JOYP per frame (test)
A malformed key token is a usage error naming the token and the grammar (test)

data.title: Read ops for sym <pattern> and checkpoints
data.description:
Why: design §12 lists `sym <pattern>` and `checkpoints` as read verbs; the server has no op for either, so the CLI can't offer them.

What: two read ops. `sym <pattern>` lists the session's symbols matching a glob (name, bank:address, region), from the .sym the session loaded. `checkpoints` lists the session's named checkpoints and history entries (name, frame since boot, rev, ROM hash match). Rows by default, `--json` the result object. Neither changes the head.

criteria.label: Each op has a server test and a CLI golden test of rows and --json

data.text:
Roster, sixth session (2026-11-06), worktrees made by hand under .claude/worktrees/ with the corpus symlinked:
- cli-agent (wt/cli): LUax7P. Owns crates/gbcli and a new CLI library crate. Does not edit server/protocol/engine.
- shot-agent (wt/shot): aAbKcV, then bHJhLp (--keys), then H9C0gs (sym/checkpoints ops) as context allows. Owns crates/server, crates/protocol, crates/engine. CLI flags for its ops come back as integration notes.
- backend-agent (wt/backend): Uks5Iy, xEga77, then RU4MNT. Owns crates/sameboy, crates/sameboy-sys, crates/corpus, test ROM sources, crates/view/tests.
Audio (aDOL0w) waits for backend-agent's merge (shared crates/sameboy and core).

User ruling, 2026-11-06 (sixth session): option A. An offset after a name is decimal in both grammars; hex needs `$` or `0x` (as RGBDS and hardware.inc read it). `rLCDC+10` is $FF4A, `rLCDC+$10` is $FF50. Design §7's "rLCDC+10 is $FF50" changes. To be implemented after shot-agent's engine work merges (it owns crates/engine now), with a test that both grammars agree.

Fixed in the backend's poke path, through a new shim accessor (no vendored-SameBoy patch, so the core identity is unchanged). `gbcli_refresh_palette_color(gb, background, index)` (crates/sameboy-sys/shim/gbcli_shim.c) calls SameBoy's internal `GB_palette_changed`, which re-converts the color holding palette-RAM byte `index` into `background_palettes_rgb`/`object_palettes_rgb`. `memory::poke` calls it for every byte poked into BgPalette/ObjPalette. `GB_palette_changed` has hidden visibility, but the shim links into the same static library, so it resolves.

Red first: `a_poked_cgb_palette_color_appears_in_the_next_frame` (crates/sameboy/tests/display.rs) pokes BG palette 0 color 0 and OBJ palette 0 color 3 on layers_cgb.gb, runs to the frame end and checks frame[0] (background) and (26,8) (object 3) against `rgb555_color`. It failed (frame[0] was 0xFFFFFF, the old white), then passed.

The view tests' `write_palette` is now `set_palette` and pokes palette RAM (crates/view/tests/common/mod.rs). Decision: pokes, because the bus route was only a workaround for this bug, the scene is a fixture rather than a test of BCPD, and with pokes the `cgb_frame_1x` golden is end-to-end coverage of this fix. All CGB goldens are byte-identical. The BCPS/BCPD path stays covered by `a_cgb_color_converts_as_the_frame_shows_it`. Gotcha entry removed.

layers_cgb.asm now turns the LCD off before its VRAM and OAM writes: if LCDC.7 is set it waits for LY >= 144 and writes LCDC=0 (LY reads 0 with the LCD off, so it checks LCDC first, or the wait would never end). Rebuilt with scripts/build-roms.sh (RGBDS 1.0.4); only layers_cgb.gb/.sym changed, every other ROM rebuilt byte-identical.

Red first: `cgb_priorities_attribute_bit_oam_flag_and_index` (crates/sameboy/tests/layers.rs) now runs under both the quick boot ROM and the fast CGB boot (new local `fast_cgb` helper). Under the fast boot it failed at (32,0): Background, expected object 1, the dropped OAM write. After the ROM fix it passes.

Under the quick boot the LCD is off at handover (power-on LCDC is 0), so the ROM skips the wait and the layer tests run exactly the old path. One existing test had to change: `a_cgb_color_converts_as_the_frame_shows_it` (display.rs, fast boot) ran 2 frames after handover; the ROM now turns the LCD off and on again, and SameBoy blanks the first frame after LCD-on (gotcha "SameBoy publishes a blank frame..."), so it now runs 3. Its assertion is unchanged.

View tests: `cgb_scene` no longer pokes OAM or the ROM's attributes back; it pokes only its own extra attribute (BG palette 1 at x=8). All view goldens are byte-identical, including cgb_frame_1x and cgb_oam_4x, so the ROM alone now produces the full scene. Gotcha entry removed.

Classified all 12; 1 is ours (not fixed: needs a Core contract decision), 11 are disputed with docboy. Written up in project/2026-11-06-docboy-baseline.md (update block at the top, corrected "after STOP" section, two new class paragraphs) and in scripts/corpus/docboy_classes.py.

Experiment (scratch, reverted): made `gbcli_pre_run` never return GBCLI_PRE_STOPPED, so GB_run steps through STOP and emulated time passes until the key, as SameBoy's own frontend does; re-ran `gbcli-corpus --suite docboy --id stop`. Result: mbc3_rtc_gb_stopped_recover fail -> pass; the other 11 (and stop_immediate_exit_joypad_interrupt) fail exactly as before.

- Ours: mbc3_rtc_gb_stopped_recover. The runner's `idle_until` skips the judge clock while the core runs no cycles in STOP, so SameBoy's RTC (advanced by emulated cycles) loses the wait. Fix needs the core to run through STOP with time passing (e.g. a RunRequest option the corpus runner sets while an input is pending). That changes the Core contract ("no time passes in STOP", crates/sameboy/tests/run.rs) and the design doc, so I queued it rather than deciding. Same question applies to the engine: an MBC3 game sitting in STOP while an agent runs N seconds currently gets no RTC time.
- Disputed (11), measured with a scratch probe from docboy's hand-over state, stepping through STOP:
  stop_read_ly_round1/2 read LY 21 (docboy expects 0/1); alt_alt_round1 reads 31 (expects 10). With the key at 20k/40k/65,536/100k T, ly_round1 reads 21 every time, so SameBoy's DMG PPU doesn't advance in STOP and no runner key timing changes the outcome.
  stop_read_stat_round1 reads $83 (expects $85).
  stop_trigger_interrupt: LYC=30 armed, STOP at line 20, 16-NOP sled after the wake; SameBoy falls through to fail (LY can't reach 30 without the PPU moving during STOP).
  dma_stop_during_transfer_timing_round1: SameBoy reads $24 (DMA done) where docboy expects $FF; OAM[$9F] was still $00 during STOP, so SameBoy's DMA pauses in STOP too, but it finishes at least one M-cycle sooner after the wake. The result was the same for every key time from 65,530 to 65,541 T.
  Not probed: ly_alt_round1/2, ly_alt_alt_round2, stat_round2/3 (siblings that differ only in NOP counts).

data.title: Let the MBC3 RTC run while the core sits in STOP
data.description: Found by RU4MNT (4db6d3f). While the core sits in STOP, no emulated time passes (the Core contract; crates/sameboy run.rs tests pin it), and the corpus runner's idle_until skips its clock. But on hardware the MBC3 RTC has its own 32 kHz crystal and keeps counting through STOP, so docboy's mbc3_rtc_gb_stopped_recover fails, and an MBC3 game parked in STOP while an agent runs N frames gets no RTC time. Decide how time passes in STOP: e.g. a RunRequest option that lets SameBoy step through STOP with cycles counted (as its own frontend does), or advancing only the RTC by the idle span. Changes the Core contract and design §2/§9; update the run.rs tests deliberately.

(SessionStore::checkpoint_rows, crates/bundle/src/listing.rs). A named checkpoint's file doesn't record its rev, so rev comes from the event log (last checkpoint op / run that saved it), absent if the log has none. Server tests: crates/server/src/handle/listing_tests.rs. Criterion bYJ is only half met: the CLI golden test of rows and --json belongs to the CLI (cli-agent's crate), not built here.

CLI built (crates/cli, gbcli-cli; binary only wires argv/env/stdio). As-built block in design §12.

Benchmark (criterion gXz): `python3 -I scripts/bench/cli-latency/run.py 200`, release build, session over the V1 test ROM with a head, Apple M1 8 CPUs, load avg 12 from other agents: `show` median 11.9 ms (p95 18.4), `read u16[wFrame]` 11.9 ms, `step` 13.0 ms; `version` (no request) 10.6 ms, so process start dominates. Under the 50 ms criterion.

Criterion dpJ: crates/gbcli/tests/cli/ — golden transcripts of every request verb in rows and --json (verbs.rows.txt, verbs.json.txt), batch both ways, help; one test per reachable error code asserting exit, code and remedy text (20 codes; mutation that blanked the remedy failed all 20). session_busy is pre-release (#[ignore], waits the 5 s lock). predicate_false, toolchain_missing, internal: no verb can produce them yet.

Findings for later leaves:
- `--json` prints the result object exactly (design §12), which has no `rev`, so JSON callers can't learn the revision to pass to --rev. Rows print `rev sN`. Needs a ruling: add rev to the result, or print the whole response.
- Ephemeral runs (ROM without a session) are not built: the handler has no session-less path; the CLI refuses with no_session and "add --session NAME".

- batch has no --atomic and no @tag forward references: the protocol has no tag field and the handler no transaction.

data.title: Review fixes: server and CLI commits 08b2258, 9021044
data.description: Independent review (sixth session) of 08b2258 and 9021044, given the code rather than the authors' reports. 10 findings; #7 (flag headings) fixed in df280f6. The rest are the two leaves below, with the main thread's rulings (two-way doors) in each.

data.title: Run checkpoints save only on success; the listing's rev, per-row errors, keys_unapplied on failure
data.description:
Review findings 1, 2, 9 and part of 10.
1. run writes a named checkpoint before the reads, the shot and the budget/wall-guard checks; when any of those then fails, the response is an error and the checkpoint was silently replaced (proved: `--checkpoint foo --read '[$DF00]'` exits 3 and foo moved). Ruling: design §11's order holds — a named checkpoint is saved only when the request succeeds, after reads and shot; a failed request saves none and its error says the checkpoint was not saved.
2. `checkpoints` takes a named checkpoint's rev from the latest logged request naming it, whether or not it saved (proved wrong after a failed run). Ruling: record the rev in the checkpoint file when it is saved (an optional header field, absent on old files); the listing reads it and says "unknown" for old files rather than guessing from the log.
9. One unreadable checkpoint or history entry fails the whole listing (exit 4). Ruling: the listing never fails for one entry; that row carries the load error.
10a. keys_unapplied is dropped on failed runs (only a warning remains), against the bHJhLp design block. Return it on failures too.

criteria.label: Each finding has a red-first test reproducing the review's scenario

data.title: CLI and session argument honesty: mismatched session flags, --rev everywhere, --from, stray bundles, remedies, silent ignores
data.description:
Review findings 3, 4, 5, 6, 8 and the rest of 10. Rulings (two-way doors):
3. --model, --seed, --sym given for an existing session that differs: refuse (usage error naming the session's values; remedy: drop the flag or name a new session). Same values: accept silently.
4. --rev: checked on every op that changes session state (checkpoint, break, watch, delete as well as run/step/restore/undo/write); a read verb given --rev is a usage error.
5. --from power-on skips the head by design (§9): fix the help text, not the behavior. --from with --at is a usage error.
6. Only an invocation that can create a session (a ROM with --session) creates .gbcli/. Every other verb with no bundle found is an environment error (exit 5) naming the directory searched and the command that creates one; `sessions` included.
8. Remedies that name commands or flags that don't exist (`gbcli doctor --core`, `--boot-rom`, `--from boot` in uninitialized_read) are rewritten to name things that exist; a test checks every remedy's `gbcli VERB` and `--flag` against the verb table.
10. Refuse rather than ignore: view --map with tiles/oam; --live with --any-frame. --frames help says what the default budget applies to; the watch recipe works as written. --dir beats GBCLI_DIR (an explicit flag wins over the environment). Design §12's `view palettes` is listed as not built in the as-built block.

data.text:
Built the A/B equivalence check as engine library code (crates/engine/src/equiv/: mod.rs, diff.rs, start.rs), not wired to server/CLI.

Findings and choices:
- compare(&a, &b, spec) works on try_clones, drops both machines' breakpoints/watches, applies the key timeline with the run loop's own Schedule (made pub(crate)), steps each side one frame (step frame, budget 2 frames), and compares the completed frame's pixels, RAM ranges resolved per side through each side's own .sym (addr::parse_on), and the APU write log.
- Audio: default compares each frame's writes as (addr, value, effect), ignoring times and PCs: optimization moves every write in time and moves the code; a write moved to another frame still diverges. AudioCompare::Timed adds ticks-since-start; Off skips.
- Start states: compare refuses machines that differ in model, seed, boot ROM, config, tick or held keys (StartMismatch). Start either from each ROM's boot handoff (no §6 involvement) or from one checkpoint restored into both, which runs §6's rebuilt-ROM rule; its refusal is correct for equivalence (moved PC routine or RAM = non-equivalent state).
- Criteria: vWd (broken optimization caught at exact frame) PASS: RIGHT@10 -> RAM wX 19 vs 20 at frame 30, pixels at frame 31 (152,0), derived from the program, not read off the emulator. jyq (equivalent rewrite passes 600 frames) PASS; the same script catches the broken build at frame 30.
- My first derivation for halt.gb was wrong (expected HALT forever to show at frame 2); the run loop reports HALT forever as soon as the CPU halts with IE=0, so it is frame 1. Test corrected, product unchanged.
- Cost: tests/equiv.rs (10 tests incl. 600-frame) ~1.0 s in the dev profile.

data.title: Profiler accounting: a root mid-routine, measure after a KEY1 write, HALT-wake and speed-switch ticks
data.description:
Review 2, findings 3, 4 and 6.
3. Profiling from a stop mid-routine makes that routine the root; its real RET finds no frame (a ret_jump), and the caller's exclusive cycles are charged to the root from then on (crates/engine/src/profile/routines.rs:134-138, :243-246). Plausible wrong rows at exit 0.
4. measure misses an arrival right after a KEY1 write: the KEY1 write filter stops the run after the writing instruction, and the next run skips the exec check on its first step (crates/engine/src/profile/measure.rs:234-238 with crates/sameboy/src/run.rs:126 `used.instructions > 0`). Inflated cycles or a Budget error at exit 0.
6. A halted CPU waking by dispatch: the step's ticks include SameBoy's HALT advance (2-4 T), and the whole step is classed Interrupt, so frame_budget and Routines count it active and charge the handler; double_speed is sampled after the step, so a speed-switching STOP converts pre-switch ticks at the new speed.

data.title: save(&self) can alias the hooks when it renders a sample: make saving sound
data.description: Review 2, findings 5 and 7. save(&self) now runs gbcli_sync_apu, which with capture on can render a sample; on_sample's guard() then makes a &mut Hooks while a safe caller may hold a shared borrow into the hooks (last_complete_frame, pixel_layers, written) — aliasing UB reachable from safe code (latent: no current caller overlaps). save also visibly mutates (apu().sync Lagging → Current), so measure/try_clone change what apu() reports on the original. And a sample rendered by save's sync is stamped with the last step's start, so AudioSamples.first can be early. Fix at the source: e.g. Core::save(&mut self) (a trait change touching engine and server callers), or a save path that renders no samples outside a run — decide and make the SAFETY comment true.

data.text:
Findings and fixes (acct-agent, worktree .claude/worktrees/acct, branch wt/acct; uncommitted):

3 (root mid-routine): Routines now tracks the root's SP. A RET/RETI reading a slot at or above it (a return address pushed before the profile began) returns from the root: open frames unwind, the old root keeps its cycles and inclusive-to-return, and the routine it returns into becomes the root, named by the return address (e.g. MainLoop+$3). 6 (HALT wake + speed): GB_cpu_run (sm83_cpu.c) advances 2-4 cycles in its halted branch before dispatch/fetch in the same step. data.title: Review fixes: profiler, verbs, raster and STOP commits
data.description: Third independent review (seventh session) of the commits since the review baseline: 4ca1701 and e011075 (profiler fixes, measure/equiv verbs; reviewer review-profiler) and c5cfbda and 65f2ffa (raster, STOP time, Core::save; reviewer review-raster). data.title: measure: a halted head isn't an arrival, the wall guard, and equiv-b's remedy
data.description:
Found by review-profiler (third review) in e011075/4ca1701. Three items, one surface (engine profile/measure.rs, server handle/run/measure.rs and equiv.rs).

1. measure counts the HALT wait in iteration 1 when the head is halted with PC at FROM. measure_on (`if !run.at(&from)`) and Runner::at treat the current PC as an arrival while the CPU is in HALT; the exec filter (crates/sameboy/src/run.rs) skips exec checks while halted, so iterations 2..N start at the real post-wake arrival. Repro (crates/engine/tests over roms/profile.gb): as halting() in tests/profile.rs, set PC to HaltLoop, step until halted, run 40,000 more ticks (PC=$018F halted); measure from $018F to $0190, 3 iterations, budget frames(10) -> samples [91392, 8, 8] ticks; expected 4 T each (the nop). Ruling (main thread, two-way door): an arrival requires the CPU to be about to execute FROM — a halted CPU has not arrived; iteration 1 starts at the wake. Record in design §11.

2. measure ignores the wall guard. Handler::measure calls machine.measure(spec); MeasureSpec/Runner carry no interrupt flag, so self.interrupt is never polled (run --measure in handle/run/probes.rs takes the same path). Design §5 (45AjcH): everything that emulates polls the flag. Repro: server Fixture::with_sym, run_frames(1), set_wall_guard(Duration::ZERO), Op::Measure{from:"Main.loop", to:"$0000", frames:Some(3000)} -> BudgetExhausted after 2.67 s; expected the wall-guard error at once (wall_guard_error).

3. The equiv divergence remedy "`gbcli restore equiv-b` to see side B" is wrong for a ROM_B side: Machine::restore rebuilds the core from the session's ROM (crates/engine/src/machine.rs ~318), so B's state runs on A's code or is refused rom_changed. Right only for patch-only sides. Make the remedy say what actually works for each kind of side.

criteria.label: measure from the instruction after a HALT, starting halted, times every iteration alike (test)
measure and run --measure answer the wall-guard error when the guard fires (test)
the equiv remedy for side B is right for ROM_B and patch sides (test)

data.text: Unconfirmed suspicions from the same review (check while in the area; file or fix only if a probe confirms): (a) --frame-budget drops the last partial frame when a run stops mid-frame (breakpoint or --to), so rows don't cover the whole run and nothing says so; (b) the root-return test `sp >= root_sp` uses root_sp from the first event — a profile from power-on (SP=$0000) or a program moving SP upward could read a computed push;ret as a root return. Also: wall-guard interrupt during equiv builds its error by hand rather than wall_guard_error (remedy text differs from run's) — align if cheap.

data.title: CGB speed-switch STOP: breakpoints after it fire, and it isn't HaltForever
data.description:
Found by review-raster (third review) in c5cfbda/65f2ffa, plus a pre-existing neighbor. One concept: a CGB speed-switch STOP is a halt that wakes on its own countdown and folds the wake into running the next instruction.

1. (regression, wrong answer) A breakpoint/exec filter on the instruction after a CGB speed-switch STOP never fires. crates/sameboy/src/run.rs:150-157 skips the exec check while `gbcli_halted && !gbcli_stopped`; the engine mirrors it at crates/engine/src/debug/decide.rs:149 (`regs.halted || in_stop()`). The premise "SameBoy never folds a wake into running that instruction" is false here: STOP with KEY1 bit0 set leaves stopped=false, halted=true, speed_switch_halt_countdown=0x20008 (sm83_cpu.c stop()); GB_advance_cycles clears halted when the countdown expires (timing.c) inside the halted branch's GB_advance_cycles(4), and the same GB_cpu_run then executes the instruction at PC (sm83_cpu.c:1703). Repro: CGB ROM `di; IE=0; P1=$30; ld a,1; ldh [KEY1],a; stop` at $015F, then `After: ld a,$99; ld [$C000],a` at $0161; quick_boot(CgbE), exec filter $0161, Budget::frames(30). Expected Candidate at $0161 with $C000=$00; observed Budget(Frames) pc=$0166, $C000=$99 (step trace: pc=$0161 halted=true, then pc=$0163 halted=false). Fix direction from the reviewer: don't skip when the countdown will expire within that step, or treat a speed-switch halt as not halted.

2. (pre-existing, wrong answer) The engine reports HaltForever at a CGB speed switch: crates/engine/src/debug/drive.rs:88-93 `halted_forever` = halted && IE&0x1F==0, but a speed-switch halt wakes on its countdown. Same ROM via cgb_machine + Machine::run(frames(30)) with a breakpoint at $0161 -> HaltForever pc=$0161; the CPU resumes after ~131k cycles. The standard switch sequence sets IE=0 first, so run stops at the switch on typical GBC games.

Also correct design §11's fWZwxe update and the run.rs comment that claim SameBoy never folds a wake into the instruction (a wrong documented cause: say it was wrong).

criteria.label: a breakpoint on the instruction after a speed-switch STOP fires before it runs, in the core filter and the engine (test)
run through a speed switch with IE=0 is not HaltForever (test)

data.title: Raster: a write on a line's start tick lands on the previous line; the timeline drops its stop
data.description:
Found by review-raster (third review) in c5cfbda.

1. (wrong answer at a one-tick boundary) A raster write landing exactly on a line's start tick is filed under the previous line with ticks_into_line == 912 while the next row starts at that same tick. crates/sameboy/src/raster.rs:801 (gbcli_ppu_line) vs on_line's stamp at :821-822: SameBoy's display state machine returns when display_cycles reaches exactly 0 (GB_SLEEP, <= 0, timing.h:27), so line N+1's callback fires on the next chunk and on_line stamps it back to the true T, but a CPU write at T still reads current_line == N. Repro: BootRom::BuiltIn CGB, cgb-acid-hell.gbc, Machine::raster(400); check every write against its row start: e.g. `write IoReg(105) pc=0x0829 at 17603760 on line 145 start 17602848 -> into 912; next row line 146 start 17603760` (BCPD writes on lines 145-147, 20+ cases). Expected 0 <= ticks_into_line < 912 (the write on line 146 at 0). No violations on dmg-acid2, cgb-acid2, five mealybug m3 ROMs, age m3-bg-scx, spsw-mode0. Correct design §11's "exact, not chunk-late" claim as wrong for this boundary.
2. (quality) Machine::raster (crates/engine/src/profile/raster.rs:510-516) drops the Stop, so a run ending early (Locked) returns a short timeline silently. run --raster (VWp0Ih) should return or record the stop.
Note: probing raster on mealybug/cgb-acid-hell needs BootRom::BuiltIn; with quick_boot they spin with the LCD off and give empty timelines.
Unconfirmed: the dedup "a CPU step writes a register at most once" would merge two real writes when SP is in FF01-FF7F during a push/dispatch; during the SGB intro GB_run calls GB_display_run without resetting cycles_since_run, so line stamps there could be wrong.

criteria.label: no raster write has ticks_into_line >= the line length on cgb-acid-hell (test)
Machine::raster reports how its run ended (test)

data.title: Research: GB Studio's asset pipeline, rgbgfx and hUGEDriver/.uge for agent-driven assets
data.description:
Why: the user wants gbcli to help agents author images and music for Game Boy games, learning from GB Studio. The image leaf (next) and a parked music leaf both depend on what this finds. Context and framing: project/2026-11-07-asset-pipeline-plan.md — verification over GUI replacement.

Questions, each answered with sources (file paths at a pinned commit, docs URLs):
- GB Studio (MIT): which hardware and engine limits does its asset pipeline check (unique background tiles, palettes per tile/scene on DMG and CGB, sprite and actor limits, 8x16 pairing, VRAM and bank budgets), what do its warnings and errors say, and which of those are true hardware limits vs GB Studio engine choices?
- rgbgfx (RGBDS 1.0.4, the pinned version): which flags give dedup, flips, tilemaps, attribute maps and palettes; what does it report when an image exceeds a limit; what is left for gbcli to check or explain?
- hUGEDriver and .uge: licenses (driver and tracker) and whether the driver can be vendored into `new`'s template; the .uge format (versions, structure) and how hard a lossless .uge <-> ASCII text conversion is; whether an existing text tracker format (e.g. a hUGETracker export, or another GB tracker's text format) could serve; how a song becomes driver data in an RGBDS build (hUGETracker's export, GB Studio's path).
- Anything else in GB Studio worth borrowing for an agentic tool (asset preview, bank packing, error wording).

Output: a dated finding in project/ answering each question, ending with a recommendation for (a) the image leaf's exact checks and messages, and (b) whether to un-park music authoring now, with the shape it should take. Effort: one session; read code and docs, don't build. Out of scope: implementing anything.
