data.title: Image assets: rgbgfx by convention in build, hardware-limit checks with remedies, and a preview
data.description:
Why: an agent producing art for a Game Boy game needs to know, in one command, whether an image fits the hardware and what it will look like — the asset equivalent of the build-error loop. Framing: project/2026-11-07-asset-pipeline-plan.md.

What: `build` converts images by convention (e.g. PNGs under `assets/` to tile data and tilemaps via rgbgfx, from PATH like the rest of RGBDS), and a limits check reports, as structured errors with remedies: unique tiles after dedup against VRAM (384 tiles) and what one map can address (256); colors per tile (4 on DMG) and palettes (8 of 4 on CGB); for sprite sheets, the 40-object and 10-per-line limits, 8x16 pairing, and VRAM left after backgrounds. Example message: "this background needs 291 unique tiles; a map addresses 256; these 35 tiles occur once". A preview renders the converted asset as the hardware will show it, through crates/view.

Already decided: RGBDS from PATH at the pinned version (plan decisions table); logic in a library crate (the build crate from leaf 7qzbqc), CLI only wires it. The research leaf fixes the exact checks and wording — read its doc first and follow its recommendation unless the code proves it wrong.

Seams: crates/build and the `build` verb (leaf 7qzbqc), crates/view for the preview. Out of scope: music; GBDK; an image editor.

criteria.label: An over-budget background and a sprite sheet over a hardware limit each come back as a structured error naming the limit and a remedy (tests)
A PNG under assets/ in a `new` project is converted by `build` and shows on screen in a screenshot test

data.text: Research done; the full finding is returned to the main thread for project/2026-11-07-asset-pipeline-research.md. Headlines: (1) GB Studio's background budgets (192 DMG / 384 CGB-only unique tiles) and sprite budgets are engine choices around UI tiles at $C0+, not hardware limits; it avoids 8x16 pairing bugs by deduplicating whole 8x16 units. (2) rgbgfx 1.0.4 catches colors per tile, palettes over 8, odd sizes, and -N overflow, but by default only warns past 256 tiles, silently makes DMG-incompatible multi-palette output without -c dmg, and -Z -u silently breaks 8x16 pairs (tilemap 00 01 02 00 observed). (3) hUGEDriver/hUGETracker: public-domain dedication (README, no LICENSE file); .uge v6 is a raw Pascal packed-record dump, 63,438 fixed bytes + 1,092 per pattern, verified by a parser that consumes 3 sample files and GB Studio's template exactly; driver measured at 1,936 B ROM0 + 100 B WRAM, hUGE_dosound 2,552-5,852 T per call (mean 3,260, n=600, sample song). (4) gbcli bug: the .sym parser rejects rgblink's exported-constant lines ("64 hUGE_NO_WAVE"), so any hUGEDriver build fails to load its symbols. Recommend un-parking music as a .uge <-> text converter plus our own .uge -> asm emitter.

data.title: Music: gbcli-music, .uge v1-v6 to and from a tracker-grid text form, with a piano roll
data.description:
Why: the user wants agents to author Game Boy music (ruling 2026-11-07). Agents can't drive hUGETracker's GUI, but they can read and write text; this leaf gives them a lossless text form of hUGETracker's `.uge` songs, so a human can compose in the tracker and an agent can edit, and vice versa. Framing and the format ruling: project/2026-11-07-asset-pipeline-plan.md (the music update); the format facts: project/2026-11-07-asset-pipeline-research.md §3 (v6 layout table, string-tail residue, the off-by-one order count, GB Studio's TypeScript v1–v6 loader at src/shared/lib/uge/ugeHelper.ts as the readable reference).

What: a library crate `gbcli-music` that reads `.uge` v1–v6 and writes v6, defines the canonical text form, converts both ways, and a CLI surface for it (e.g. `gbcli song to-text|to-uge`, or whatever cli-design.md and the verb table suggest), plus a piano-roll PNG rendered from a song file without building (reuse crates/audio's piano roll rendering if it fits, or share its drawing code).

Already decided (the format ruling): a tracker grid — an explicit row number on every row; the four channels as columns; cells in the XM paste convention (`C-5 01 ... 2FF`: note, instrument, volume placeholder, effect code + parameter); instruments named, with readable fields (duty, envelope, length, sweep, wave, noise mode) and their 64-row subpatterns, not register bytes; waves as 32 hex nibbles; orders per channel referencing patterns by name; routines as text blocks; one canonical output spelling (all 64 rows; hUGETracker's hex effect codes) and a `help` topic listing the effects. The exact syntax is the builder's call within that — write a short spec into the design doc and a worked example into `help`.

Tests: text → .uge → text is a fixpoint on hUGETracker's sample songs (public domain; commit them with their source and dedication), and .uge → text → .uge matches byte for byte except ShortString tails and the dead fields the research names. Parse errors are structured (line, column, message, remedy).

Seams: new crate; crates/audio for the piano roll; crates/cli verbs. Out of scope: the RGBDS emitter and build integration (music-build), a MOD importer, GBDK C output, an MML layer.
Risks: the format's dead/legacy fields; v1–v5 upgrade rules (follow GB Studio's loader and hUGETracker's song.pas).

data.title: Music: song to RGBDS emitter, build by convention, hUGEDriver in new, and the listen recipe
data.description:
Why: an agent-authored song must get into a ROM and be checked by ear-equivalents in one loop: edit the song, build, run, read the audio log and piano roll. Framing: project/2026-11-07-asset-pipeline-plan.md (music update); facts: project/2026-11-07-asset-pipeline-research.md §3 (hUGEDriver public-domain dedication, its cost: ~1.9 KB ROM0, 100 B WRAM, ~2.5–5.9k T per call on the sample song; TimerEnabled songs need the timer interrupt; hUGETracker's RenderSongToRGBDSAsm in codegen.pas:394–584).

What: (1) our own song → RGBDS `.asm` emitter in gbcli-music, a port of RenderSongToRGBDSAsm (no FPC dependency), pinned against hUGETracker's own export of the sample songs (goldens, or `equiv` on sound-register writes over N frames). (2) `build` converts `assets/music/*.uge` and the text form by convention (build crate from leaf 7qzbqc). (3) `new` can vendor hUGEDriver at a pinned commit (record the dedication, commit and SHA in a SOURCE file) with a player stub calling hUGE_dosound from the right interrupt, and its cost in the docs. (4) A recipe: build, then `run --frames N --audio-log --piano` (and per-channel `--wav`).

Seams: crates/music (music-text), crates/build and the `build`/`new` verbs (7qzbqc), crates/audio. Out of scope: MOD import, GBDK C, an MML layer.

data.title: Frame budget: show the frame in progress when a run stops mid-frame
data.description:
Found by review-profiler (third review) as a suspicion; confirmed by a probe in leaf dg4BWI, not fixed because it needs a choice that changes the wire format and CLI rows.

The problem: `run --frame-budget` drops the frame in progress when a run stops mid-frame (a breakpoint, `--to`, `--instructions`). A 5,000-instruction run inside one frame returned `frame_budget frames=0`; a 30,000-instruction run that stopped at line 20 returned six rows with nothing for the partial frame, and no output said so. The rows then don't cover the run's cycles. Recorded in design §11's dg4BWI correction.

Options: (a) a final row marked partial (its lag undefined: null), so rows sum to the run; (b) no row, but a field on the summary naming the uncounted cycles; (c) leave it and document it. Recommended: (a) — an agent summing rows should get the run's total, and "partial" is honest about lag. The builder's call if nothing new turns up; it is a two-way door before any user depends on the rows.

criteria.label: a run stopped mid-frame reports its partial frame so rows cover the run's cycles (server test and CLI golden)

data.title: build, doctor (and new) as server ops, so serve and batch can build and the CLI holds no decisions
data.description:
Found integrating 7qzbqc. `build`, `new` and `doctor` are answered in the CLI process (crates/cli/src/rgbds.rs), not as server ops, so a client driving `gbcli serve` or `batch -F` can't build, and two decisions live in the adapter: build-then-restore orchestration, and the check that the session's ROM is the file just built (else bad_request). The principle (AGENTS.md, Library + thin executable): an adapter that holds a decision is a bug.

What: `build` (and `doctor`; `new` too if it fits) become protocol ops handled by the server calling gbcli-build, with the restore-after-build and the session-ROM check in the server, so serve, batch and the CLI share one path; the CLI keeps only argv parsing and rendering. Results already are protocol types (crates/protocol/src/toolchain.rs), so the wire shape exists.
Open question for the builder: whether `new` (which writes a directory and touches no session) belongs on the wire; say what you chose and why.

data.title: Build loop review fixes: session-safe names, color, relative PATH, staging tests, gitignore, remedy, macro chains
data.description:
Independent review (review-build, seventh session) of 56159fc. Confirmed findings, each with its reproduction:

1. (wrong answer) `new` accepts names a session can't take, so its printed next command fails. crates/build/src/scaffold.rs `plain` check allows `_`, `.`, uppercase; session names are [a-z0-9-]{1,40}. `gbcli new my-game_2` prints `gbcli run … --session my-game_2`, which is bad_request exit 2; also `my.game`, `MyGame`. BadName's message claims `_` and `.` are fine. The README template's `--session {{name}}` breaks the same way. Fix: either derive a valid session name (e.g. lowercase, `_`/`.` → `-`) for the printed commands, or refuse such names with a remedy — say which and why.
2. (wrong answer) FORCE_COLOR in the environment breaks every diagnostic: crates/build/src/project.rs Run::step never passes `--color never`; RGBDS 1.0.4 colors when FORCE_COLOR is set even piped. `env FORCE_COLOR=1 gbcli build <proj with errors>` → every row is the fallback with ESC codes and no line. Pass `--color never` to all three tools (check each accepts it at 1.0.4).
3. (robustness) A relative PATH entry: doctor ok, build io_failed. toolchain.rs `find` returns dir.join(file) unresolved; Run::step runs it with current_dir(project). `PATH=rb gbcli doctor` ok; `PATH=rb gbcli build w1/game` → io_failed "rb/rgbasm: No such file". Resolve against the cwd at discovery.
4. (test passes for the wrong reason) tests/build.rs `a_failed_build_leaves_the_last_good_rom_in_place` fails in rgbasm before staging exists; a mutation writing the real ROM inside `if !fixed {` passed every test. Add link-failure and rgbfix-failure cases.
5. (wrong warning) doctor's gitignore check matches six exact spellings; misses ignored parents, `**/.gbcli`, .git/info/exclude, global excludes. From target/rv in this repo it warns though `git check-ignore -v` shows `/target/` ignores it. Use `git check-ignore -q` when git is available (fall back as now otherwise).
6. (quality) build_failed's default remedy says "then `gbcli build` again" without the project directory (crates/protocol/src/error.rs), wrong when the build named one. Name the directory the build used.
7. (quality) Macro/include call sites (`<-` frames) and rgblink's second location ("and also: at …") are dropped (diagnostics.rs; Diagnostic has no field). An agent can't tell which invocation failed. Add the chain to Diagnostic (protocol type; rows and --json).

Unconfirmed suspicions worth settling while there: `build/.staging` removed unconditionally — with `--out game.gb` that's `<project>/.staging`, possibly the user's, and concurrent builds share it (use a unique staging dir under build/ or beside the ROM with a gbcli-specific name); ROM/.sym/.map renamed one by one (a load between pairs the new ROM with the old .sym; consider renaming .sym/.map first and the ROM last, so the ROM's arrival marks completion); `brew install rgbds` installs Homebrew's current release, not the pin (say so in the remedy and give the pinned-release URL first); no timeout on tool runs; a symlink loop under src/ is followed.

data.title: Build crate: kill a hung tool's process group, full and quoted remedies, refuse --out colliding with .sym/.map, sweep stale staging
data.description:
Found by review-build (2026-11-07) in e3ca2be. Probes in crates/build/tests/review_probes.rs (reviewer's file, all red):

1 (medium) The tool time limit kills only the direct child; a wrapper script (version-manager shim, sh without exec) leaves the real tool as a grandchild holding stderr, and reader.join() blocks until it exits, so a hung build never returns and the orphan outlives it (project.rs 411-418, 492-505). Probe probe_a_wrapped_tool_that_hangs_is_still_stopped_on_time (fake rgbasm `sleep 5` without exec, 0.2 s limit: took 10.03 s). Fix: own process group per tool, kill the group on timeout, never block unbounded on the reader after a kill.
2 (low) A failed build's remedy drops --src/--include/--out (project.rs 107-114). Probe probe_a_failed_builds_remedy_keeps_the_layout_flags_it_was_built_with.
3 (low) Commands printed by new and the build remedy are not shell-quoted: new "my games/demo" prints `gbcli build my games/demo` (scaffold.rs 97-110, project.rs 107-110). Probes probe_new_prints_next_commands_a_shell_can_run, probe_a_failed_builds_remedy_is_a_command_a_shell_can_run.
4 (low) --out ending .sym or .map collides with its own .sym/.map; rgblink gets one path for -o and -n; io_failed with an unhelpful message (project.rs 180-188, 217-222). Fix: refuse as bad_request before any tool runs. Probe probe_an_out_that_collides_with_its_own_sym_is_refused.
5 (noted, fold in) A killed build skips Staging Drop, so .gbcli-staging-<pid>-<n> dirs pile up (project.rs 256-260), in the project root when --out puts the ROM there. Remove stale staging dirs whose pid is not alive at the next build.

criteria.label: the five review probes pass (tests)
a killed build's staging dir is removed by the next build (test)

data.title: build --restore: the server checks the session before building and refuses restore-only fields without restore
data.description:
Found by review-build (2026-11-07, by trace) in e3ca2be. (a) The CLI opens the session before building and fails no_session (crates/cli/src/exec.rs 71-74); serve builds and replaces the ROM first, then refuses (crates/server/src/handle/build.rs 102 then 132). (b) The CLI refuses --rev, --session and --allow-rom-change without --restore (crates/cli/src/rgbds.rs); the server ignores them (build.rs 106).

Ruling (main thread, two-way door): the server holds the decision. It checks the restore target session exists before running any tool, and refuses rev/session/allow_rom_change without restore as bad_request, so CLI and serve answer the same request the same way; the CLI then keeps no copy of either check (library + thin adapter).

data.title: Music crate: even orders, piano follows hUGEDriver's 7xx/Exx, canonical missing patterns, v7 message, subpattern range, strict numbers
data.description:
Found by review-music (2026-11-07) in 1a4bfdc, checked against hUGETracker 3fedced3 and hUGEDriver 727ab8e sources. Probes: scratchpad music-review_probes.rs (was crates/music/tests/review_probes.rs; 8 red). Run with GBCLI_TEST_ROMS=/Users/ben/git/gbcli/tests/corpus/fetched.

1 (medium) Uneven channel orders (`-` once a shorter list ends) have no meaning in hUGETracker: its save pads every channel to RowCount (tracker.pas 998-1013), load shows missing cells as pattern 0 (1016-1045), and export sets OrderCnt to the longest list while writing each shorter array, so the driver reads into the next channel's table (codegen.pas 391-398). The piano walks only the shortest channel (piano.rs:94 .min()). Probe probe_uneven_orders_play_to_the_longest_channel. RULING (main thread): the text form refuses uneven orders with a located parse error and a remedy (every channel needs the same number of orders; name a pattern for each); drop `-` from the grammar, help and design §12 (correct in place); the piano walks all orders.
2 (medium-low) Piano roll diverges from hUGEDriver for 7xx and Exx: 700 never plays the note, delay >= row ticks skips it (fx_note_delay ~1360-1372); Exx cuts only when the tick counter equals xx, so xx >= ticks never fires (fx_note_cut ~899). piano.rs 123-127, 146. Probes probe_piano_note_delay_700_never_plays_the_note, probe_piano_note_delay_past_the_row_never_plays_the_note, probe_piano_note_cut_past_the_row_does_not_cut.
3 (low) piano.rs:180 usize::try_from(instrument - 1) overflows on i32::MIN (panic in dev/test). Probe probe_piano_survives_instrument_i32_min. checked_sub.
4 (low) An order naming a missing pattern gains a blank one through text (write.rs patterns(), BLANK_ROWS). Probe probe_order_naming_a_missing_pattern_adds_one. RULING: normalize on read the way hUGETracker does (GetOrCreateNew): the reader creates the blank pattern, so the model is canonical and round trips are equal.
5 (low) read_song (lib.rs:53-58) sends a .uge with version > 6 to the text parser, so read_uge's "newer hUGETracker" message is unreachable. Probe probe_a_v7_uge_says_its_version_through_read_song.
6 (low, docs) Subpattern rows 32-63 and jumps J32-J64 never play (SubpatternToBytes exports rows 0-31; do_table's jump is 5 bits) but help/remedies say J01-J64 (instrument.rs:166). RULING: keep storing all 64 rows (lossless); help and remedies state that only rows 00-31 play and jumps reach J01-J31 (check the exact bound against the driver); `song` warns when a subpattern has content past row 31 or a jump past the playable range.
7 (low) Parser accepts `\x+F` (lex.rs:93 from_str_radix takes a leading +), `+7`, and wave bytes `+F`; `length !N` stores max-N (instrument.rs:233 steps) contradicting spell.rs (`!N` is its stored number). Probe probe_text_escape_with_plus_sign_is_refused. Refuse signs; make !N the stored number.
8 (trivial) lib.rs:1 says v1-v6; it reads v0 too.

criteria.label: the eight red review probes pass (tests)
song warns on subpattern content past the playable rows (test)

data.text: Red (all 9 new/renamed tests failed as expected), then green: tool runs in own process group (std process_group(0)) and the group is killed via the POSIX kill utility (workspace forbids unsafe; no dependency); stderr reader bounded by a 500 ms grace via mpsc recv_timeout. Remedy repeats --src/--include/--out, shell-quoted (paths::quote). --out .sym/.map is a Layout refusal. Staging dirs hold a flock'd lock file (std File::lock); the next build sweeps dirs whose lock it can take.

Findings so far (mappers):
- GB_reset keeps cart RAM only on battery carts (reset_ram memsets mbc_ram to 0xFF when !has_battery) and keeps the rtc section, but it is not deterministic for us: reset_ram draws WRAM from SameBoy's process-global GB_random (no reseed) and stamps last_rtc_second = time(NULL). So gbcli's power cycle rebuilds the core under the construction lock (seeded) and carries the battery across as a .sav, not GB_reset.
- GB_load_battery_from_buffer reads time(NULL) twice and advances the clock by host time since the stamp (or resets it with the 0x80 hint if the stamp is <1997 or in the future); it can't be neutralized from outside, so shim/gbcli_battery.c reads the MBC3 footer itself (vba64 48 B and vba32 44 B). HuC3/TPP1 footers refused as Unsupported for now.

data.title: gbcli doesn't report the LCD being turned off outside VBlank
data.description:
Found while writing the `traps` help topic (leaf shsW4F). Turning the LCD off (LCDC bit 7 1 -> 0) outside VBlank can damage a real DMG's screen (Pan Docs, https://gbdev.io/pandocs/LCDC.html#lcdc7--lcd-enable), but gbcli says nothing: no warning, no stop reason, no gap entry. The vendored SameBoy has a `lcd_disabled_outside_of_vblank` field (gb.h:544) that is only ever reset (display.c:189), never set, and its debugger, which is compiled out, has no such warning either.

What an agent can see today: `gbcli run --frames 4 --raster` lists the rLCDC write under the line it landed on (the demo crates/gbcli/tests/traps/lcd_off.gb shows line 60, then 144). The help topic says so and says gbcli does not warn.

Possible fix: a warning on the run (and the stop?) when LCDC bit 7 goes 1 -> 0 with LY < 144, from the IO-write hook the raster timeline already uses; or a watch-style stop reason. Decide whether it is a warning (exit 0) or something stronger.

data.title: run --to that ends on illegal_opcode exits 0 without reaching its target
data.description:
Found while writing the OAM DMA trap demo (leaf shsW4F). `gbcli run --to AfterRomDma --frames 30` on crates/gbcli/tests/traps/dma_rom.gb never reaches AfterRomDma: the CPU runs off into VRAM and hits an illegal opcode. The run stops with reason `illegal_opcode` (pc=$8014) and exits 0 with `"ok": true`.

A run with a target (--to, --until) that ends without reaching it because the budget ran out fails with budget_exhausted (exit 3). Ending because the CPU locked up is the same "the target was never reached", yet it reads as success to a script branching on the exit code — a plausible wrong answer (cli-design ▸ Errors that teach). Check which other stop reasons (stop instruction? wall guard?) end a targeted run with exit 0, and decide the code (3, with the stop attached, like budget_exhausted?).

The traps test (crates/gbcli/tests/cli/traps.rs, oam_dma_from_rom_runs_wild_and_from_hram_returns) asserts the stop reason and pc, and currently expects exit 0; it will need its expected exit code changed with the fix.

data.title: Region offsets: the condition grammar reads sram:10 as decimal where the address grammar reads hex
data.description:
Found by the mappers agent (OU9rOL, 2026-11-07): the address grammar reads a region offset as hex, prefixed or not (`poke sram:10=$AB` writes offset $10, design §7), but the condition grammar reads the same text as decimal (`read '[sram:10]'` reads offset $0A, with an uninitialized-read warning). Recorded in project/gotchas.md.

Ruling (main thread, two-way door): design §7 governs: a region offset is hex in both grammars. Fix the condition grammar, with a test that poke-then-read of sram:10 agrees, and remove the gotcha.

data.title: Battery saves: bound --rtc-advance, and let power-cycle keep a HuC3/TPP1 battery
data.description:
Found by review-battery (2026-11-07) in a066271. Probes kept in the session scratchpad battery-probes/ (copy them into the next agent's brief; scratch may not survive): sameboy_review_battery_probe.rs (probe_a_huge_advance_after_any_elapsed_second_is_a_silent_no_op, probe_advance_cost_is_linear_in_days, probe_huc3_round_trip_is_refused), engine_review_battery_probe.rs (probe_huc3_power_cycle_keep). Path: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ben-git-gbcli/e010e3ab-3a8d-446a-8cef-664e9ece2891/scratchpad/battery-probes/

1 (medium-low) --rtc-advance is unbounded: parse_duration (crates/bundle/src/prune.rs:64) accepts up to u64::MAX s; gbcli_battery.c:57 adds last_rtc_second + seconds, which wraps (silent no-op that still reports rtc_advanced_s), and GB_rtc_set_time (Core/timing.c:369) loops once per day, ~2.7 ns/day: 99999999999d holds the session lock ~4.5 min, the max ~6.6 days. Fix: refuse past a stated bound (the MBC3 day counter is 9 bits + carry, so >512 days all read alike: cap or refuse with that remedy) and use checked addition in the shim.
2 (low) On HuC3/TPP1 every power-cycle is refused (Battery::Keep round-trips through the import, which refuses their footers; machine/power.rs:41-52). Fix: when no --sav is given, carry the old core's battery bytes without parsing the footer, or document the refusal in help and §6 (now corrected to say so).

1. MEDIUM-HIGH. Colors equal in RGB555 build with wrong shades. rgbgfx reduces to RGB555; gbcli counts/shades 24-bit colors. #040404 and #000000 get separate indices in gbcli, one in rgbgfx (warning only). In a sprite, a black pixel draws white; in a background tile, black comes out dark gray; across tiles the cross-check fires with a confusing message. data.title: Music build: ROM-only overflow past bank 1, 6xx routine table, routine label scope, dotted stems, _TIMER collisions, timer-song docs
data.description:
Findings from review-music on 1ffe1f6 (pukTN6's landed part). Probes: scratchpad/probes/review_probes_music.rs (crates/build/tests; 5 probes, all red; `cargo test -p gbcli-build --test review_probes_music`). The reviewer diffed the emitter against codegen.pas at 0623f3f7 by hand and found the port faithful; every finding is around it.

1. HIGH. Songs past bank 1 play another song's data, silently. Each song is its own SECTION ROMX (asm.rs:55); the starter is ROM-only (rgbfix with no -m); when songs pass 16 KB, rgblink places one in bank 2 and makes a 64 KB ROM with no diagnostic, and a ROM-only cart can't map bank 2. Probe: probe_a_song_past_bank_1_still_plays_or_fails_the_build. Two of hUGETracker's samples together (FADE 12.9 KB + Wyrmhole 8.0 KB) already overflow.
   RULING (main thread, two-way door): fix at the source in build, for any section, not only songs: a ROM whose header names no MBC (cart type $00/$08/$09) and whose link needs more than 32 KB fails with a structured build error naming the sections placed past bank 1 (from the .map) and a remedy (shrink, or choose an MBC in the header and switch banks around the code that reads them). The starter stays ROM-only.
2. MEDIUM-HIGH. Effect 6xx freezes the game: hUGEDriver's fx_call_routine (hUGEDriver.asm:719-743) reads a dw pointer from [routines]+2n, but the export writes routine code directly at routines: (asm.rs:109-117, faithful to codegen.pas:618-627). Probe: probe_effect_6xx_runs_its_routine.
   RULING (two-way door): make 6xx work: emit a dw table of routine pointers at routines:, then the routines. First check how hUGETracker's own preview/ROM path does it (codegen.pas:758, the routineN.htt template) and follow that. Record the departure from the RGBDS export in project/2026-11-07-music-build.md ("departures"), and exclude 6xx-using songs from the byte/register comparison against hUGETracker's export or compare with that difference stated.
3. MEDIUM. Two routines with the same local label don't assemble: the port scopes __hUGE_Routine_N under the song (song_theme.__hUGE_Routine_0:), which opens no new scope, so every .loop becomes song_theme.loop. Give each routine its own global label, unique per song. The music-build doc's claim that the scoping "doesn't change a byte" must be corrected (it changes which songs assemble). Probe: probe_two_routines_with_the_same_local_label_build.
4. MEDIUM-LOW. music.rs:92 out_dir.join(stem).with_extension("asm"): theme.v2.song writes build/music/theme.asm over theme's. Probe: probe_a_dotted_stem_gets_its_own_asm.
5. LOW. theme_TIMER.song collides with theme's exported song_theme_TIMER constant; the duplicate check (music.rs:64) knows labels only. Check every exported symbol (labels, _TIMER, _TMA). Probe: probe_a_stem_ending_in_timer_builds.
6. LOW, docs. With a timer-driven song, a timer tick running at VBlank delays the VBlank handler: OAM DMA landed on lines 145-153 in 16 of 600 frames (`gbcli new`, add `timer on 192` to theme.song, `run --frames 600 --raster`). Say so in help music (timer songs can push VBlank work late; the cost per tick) - no code change.
7. LOW. every_effect.song uses only effects 0,1,2,3,4,A,B,E: no 5-9, C, D, F, no subpattern. Rename it or extend it; pukTN6's criterion r4P (a song of reasonable complexity) is the place to extend it.

data.title: Run and onboarding: SGB LCD-off toggles, --to an illegal opcode, opcode lookup's RGBDS spellings, ticks wording, frame numbering, %-offsets
data.description:
Findings from review-run on 4aa3996 (XStY5L, k56pRp, jXavVc) and 8c1f5de (shsW4F, pa2Jwt). Probes: scratchpad/probes/review_probes_run.rs and review_probes_opcode.rs (crates/engine/tests). The FFI/lifetime side was checked and found sound.

1. MEDIUM (4aa3996). The LCD-off warning is wrong on SGB. SameBoy writes LCDC three times for one program write on SGB (GB_CONFLICT_SGB_LCDC, sm83_cpu.c:248-258: value, old, value), so an LCD-off fires the callback off->on->off; the last off reads gbcli_ppu_line after GB_lcd_off reset current_line to 0 (display.c:596) and overwrites hooks.lcd_off_line (raster.rs:94-97). Every SGB LCD-off reports line 0 (so a legal VBlank one warns), and every turn-on logs as an off. Probe: probe_sgb_lcd_off_warning_matches_dmg (lcd_off demo on Model::Sgb gets pc $015C, line 0, more 2; expected line 60, more 0). DMG and CGB conflict paths don't toggle.
2. MEDIUM (4aa3996). `run --to X` exits 3 (target_not_reached, "PC never reached X") when PC does reach X, if X holds an illegal opcode: the core checks GBCLI_PRE_ILLEGAL (sameboy/src/run.rs:135) before the exec filter (:154). Same ordering makes a session breakpoint on an illegal byte report illegal_opcode, not the breakpoint (predates the commit). `--until "pc == X"` is fine. Probe: probe_to_an_address_holding_an_illegal_opcode_is_reached (control probe_until_pc_at_an_illegal_opcode_holds is green).
3. LOW-MEDIUM (8c1f5de). `gbcli opcode` matches operands as a prefix: `xor a` returns all 9 xor forms instead of $AF; `cp 5` and `sub b` (RGBDS short ALU forms, the common spelling) are bad_request; `ld a, (hl)` silently matches ld a, n8 ($3E). Also `ld [c], a` / `ld [$ff00+c], a` find nothing (token() maps to [c] but only ldh has that form), and `ldi`/`ldd` are unknown. Accept exactly what rgbasm 1.0.4 accepts (check each spelling against rgbasm), match exactly, and refuse what it refuses with a remedy. Probes: review_probes_opcode.rs (both red).
4. LOW (8c1f5de). help hardware says "gbcli counts T-cycles (t, measure, --ticks)", but ticks are 2^23 Hz, two per T-cycle at single speed (crates/core/src/time.rs:3-6). Repro: `gbcli run crates/gbcli/tests/traps/halt_bug.gb --session s --ticks 1000 --json` stops at t 508, budget.ticks 1016.
5. LOW, SUSPECTED (4aa3996). The LCD-off warning numbers frames from core.vblanks, while stop records number them from the last published frame, and a CGB repeat vblank is never published (hooks.rs around 270). Confirm with a probe; fix if they disagree, or record why not.
6. LOW (4aa3996). A condition reads [sram:%10] as binary 2 (the lexer marks % numbers as prefixed); the address grammar refuses %10. Make the condition grammar refuse it too, the same way.

data.title: Second-review fixes: 16-bit PNG decode and an index cross-check, frame-size remedy names, opcode lookup's missing commas and expressions, routine-label note
data.description:
Findings from the second review (ninth session) of the fix commits cd55e6f (JAzaVy), d5c4442 (dwM7t6), 949470b (pruzN6). Probes: scratchpad/probes/review2_probes_images.rs (crates/build/tests; 2 red) and review2_probes_lookup.rs (crates/engine/tests; 1 red, lists every disagreement with rgbasm).

A1 MEDIUM (images). pixels.rs reads 16-bit PNGs with STRIP_16 (high byte); rgbgfx 1.0.4 rounds 16-bit to 8-bit. So gbcli's RGB555 keys can differ from rgbgfx's: an 8x8 16-bit gray bg with a white row and pixels $07FF and $0800 is planned as 3 colors (white 0, $08 -> 2, $07 -> 3) but rgbgfx merges them and writes index 2 where the plan says 3; the build succeeds. Probe review2_a_16_bit_png_is_shaded_as_gbcli_planned. Fix at the source: decode 16-bit as rgbgfx does (check its rounding in rgbgfx's source/behavior). Also: run.rs checks only the sizes of rgbgfx's output, never the color indices against gbcli's own units; add that cross-check so any future decode disagreement fails the build loudly (fail closed) instead of building wrong shades.
A2 LOW (images). find.rs source(): the bad-frame-size check runs before the name check and its remedy reuses the raw stem: assets/sprites/2hero.big.png -> "rename it to 2hero.WxH.png", itself an invalid label. Probe review2_a_bad_frame_size_remedy_offers_a_valid_name.
B1 LOW (opcode lookup). `written` strips whitespace, so `jr nz Top` becomes the one operand `nzTop` (data) and answers unconditional jr e8 ($18); rgbasm refuses it. Same for `call z Top`, `jp c Top`.
B2 LOW (opcode lookup). Refuses lines rgbasm accepts: high/low of a register pair (`ld a, high(bc)` $78, `ld a, low(hl)`, `ld [hl], low(de)`, `ld a, high(af)` $7F) and constant expressions in rst/bit numbers (`rst 8*7` $FF, `bit 3+4, a` CB 7F, `set 2*3, [hl]`). Probe review2_more_spellings_agree_with_rgbasm (B1+B2).
C1 LOW, SUSPECTED, docs only: routine code naming hUGETracker's own __hUGE_Routine_N / __end_hUGE_Routine_N labels now fails at link (renamed song_x__...). Loud, not wrong data. Say so in help music / the music-build doc's departures.

data.title: Battery and OAM review: the advance bound per mapper, raw-OAM wording, palette in CGB rows
data.description:
Findings from the review (ninth session) of e65e509 (l1ql7D, 3LC83k). Nothing serious: shim buffer arithmetic, sizes and round trips for every cart shape, determinism across power cycles and checkpoints, and the OAM parser all checked sound. Probes saved at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ben-git-gbcli/b678e931-d90c-4bb0-80e2-01b9d475c9fc/scratchpad/probes/review3_probes_battery.rs (crates/sameboy/tests; 2 red), review3_probes_power.rs and review3_probes_oam.rs (crates/engine/tests; green checks worth keeping). The scratchpad may not survive; the findings are restated here.

1. LOW. The 1024-day bound's "no reading lost" claim holds for MBC3 only. TPP1 counts 256 weeks (1792 days) before its MR4 overflow, so weeks 147-255 and the overflow flag aren't reachable in one advance from week 0. HuC3's day counter is 16-bit (SameBoy timing.c:352). Red probes: probe_tpp1_an_advance_past_512_days_reads_like_one_512_days_shorter (weeks 214 vs 141 for 1500d vs 988d) and probe_huc3_... (days $5DC vs $3DC). Nothing is truly lost, since chained cycles reach them. Fix: either a per-mapper bound (MBC3 1024 d, TPP1 its 1792 d plus 1792 for the flag, HuC3 a host-time-cost bound), or keep one bound and correct the claim in MAX_RTC_ADVANCE_S's doc, design §6 (whose "reaching its wrap is not supported" for HuC3 is wrong: 64 chained cycles reach it; TPP1 is unmentioned) and the error texts (crates/sameboy/src/battery.rs, crates/server/src/handle/battery.rs), which explain a HuC3/TPP1 refusal in MBC3 terms.
2. LOW, docs. oam[N].field reads raw OAM, not what the CPU sees: in mode 3 the CPU reads $FF at $FE01 while oam[0].x = 1. That is consistent with every expression read, but help expressions and the §7 update don't say so for OAM, where it matters most (modes 2/3, OAM DMA).
3. LOW. In CGB mode the oam[N] row still prints `palette` (bit 4, "Non CGB Mode only" in Pan Docs) beside cgb_palette. Omit it in CGB mode, or label it.
4. VERY LOW, SUSPECTED. inspect/video.rs object_attributes treats a color_mode() error as DMG silently. SameBoy never errors there; it's a risk for other backends only.

criteria.label: the TPP1 and HuC3 probes pass, or the claim is corrected everywhere it is made (test or doc)

RULING (Ben, 2026-11-07): option 2 for DMG shades. Each color takes the DMG shade nearest its lightness, even when two colors then share a shade (hardware allows it: BGP/OBP can map two indices to one shade). When two or more colors share a shade, the build warns: it names the colors, the shade and where they are, and remedies "make them distinct if the difference matters". More colors than the hardware takes (4 for a background; 3 plus transparent for a sheet) stays an error (dmg_palette), naming the extra colors and their tiles. That already holds; keep a test for it.

Today, shades.rs spreads colors that would share a shade lightest-to-darkest, so black + #101010 draws #101010 as white, silently. Replace that. Update help images, design §12 (a dated ruling block) and the shades.rs unit tests: the near-white pair test pins the old rule.

criteria.label: black plus #101010 builds with both black and a warning naming both colors (test)
a background with 5 colors, or a sheet with 4 opaque colors, is a dmg_palette error naming the extras (test)

data.title: GBC images in dual mode: research GB Studio's approach, then plan --gbc
data.description:
Why: an agent making a Game Boy Color game needs color art in the same build loop as DMG art. Today build has no GBC target, so it always builds for DMG; the CGB-images item in project/backlog.md (2026-11-07) is parked for that reason, and is un-parked by this.

RULINGS (Ben, 2026-11-07):
- A flag picks the target: `gbcli build --gbc`. Use "GBC" in user-facing names; Pan Docs and rgbfix say CGB (`rgbfix -C` is GBC-only, `-c` is dual mode), so map the names in the docs.
- Dual mode is the goal: a GBC-enhanced ROM that still runs on the original Game Boy. Every image then needs a color version for GBC and a 4-shade version for DMG.
- Where the gray version comes from is open: research GB Studio's approach first.

This leaf is the research and the plan, not the build. What to find out:
1. How GB Studio handles color (GBC) art and its DMG fallback: are DMG shades derived from the color image, from a separate image, or chosen by hand per palette? How does it assign palettes per tile or per actor, and what are the limits and the UI around them? Read its source (github.com/chrismaltby/gb-studio: its image and palette compilers) and docs; cite files and lines.
2. How GB Studio picks sprite transparency (its key color vs alpha) and whether its color art uses the same rule. Context: gbcli uses true alpha and plans to keep it; a hint for GB Studio green is a candidate.
3. rgbgfx 1.0.4's behavior for -c/-m/-a/-p with more than 8 palettes, and how it packs tiles into palettes (which tiles force a ninth), so gbcli's own check can name them.
4. What a dual-mode build needs beyond images: the header (rgbfix -c), the starter detecting the GBC at boot (A = $11) and loading palettes, the VRAM bank 1 attribute map, and what `run`/screenshots need (the session model on GBC).

Output: a dated research doc under project/, then a plan doc with a tasks: block (project/agents/planning.md) for Ben to review before any building. Recommend a gray-version strategy with its tradeoffs (derived from color by nearest shade per palette, a separate `name.dmg.png`, or GB Studio's way).

criteria.label: a dated research doc answers questions 1-4 with sources
a plan doc with a tasks: block is ready for Ben's review
